AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1324 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed.
  • For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works.
  • But the latest findings raise an vital question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A newly introduced study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.

For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.

But the latest findings raise an vital question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?

Sources indicate that "Artificial intelligence systems are often described as 'brain-like' because they can predict activity in parts of the brain that help us recognize objects," says York University Assistant Professor Kohitij Kar, senior author of a upcoming study. "Until now, scientists mostly tested this in one direction. They asked whether AI models can predict brain activity.".

A Fresh Test Reveals a Hidden Problem With Brain-Like AI.

The York University team decided to approach this question from the opposite direction. Rather than simply measuring how well AI could predict the activity of brain cells, they investigated whether recorded brain activity could also predict what was happening inside the AI models.

If these systems truly operate like the brain, the researchers reasoned, the relationship should work in both directions. To investigate, they developed a method called reverse predictivity testing, which allowed them to evaluate similarities that conventional tests could overlook.

"Ultimately, we need computational models to truly understand the underlying neural mechanisms of how we recognize objects. How do we see objects move? While it's a very easy task that we do every day, computationally, though, it's a very challenging problem," notes Kar, the Canada Research Chair in Visual Neuroscience and a member of York's Centre for Vision Research and Centre for Integrative and Applied Neuroscience.

The research team, which included York Postdoctoral Fellow Sabine Muzellec, a trainee with the university's Connected Minds program, examined responses to a wide variety of visual images.

Their tests included 1,320 natural photographs and realistic synthetic images featuring 10 familiar subjects: a bear, an elephant, a face, an apple, a car, a dog, a chair, a plane, a bird, and a zebra. These objects appeared against a variety of natural scenes and indoor or outdoor backgrounds. The researchers also introduced 300 additional images showing the same subjects in different visual styles, including outlines, drawings, simplified representations, and artistic interpretations.

AI Can Predict Brain Activity, but the Reverse Tells a Different Story.

The results revealed a significant disconnect between artificial intelligence and biological vision.

AI models were generally successful at predicting the responses of recorded neurons, which are the specialized cells that transmit information throughout the brain. However, when the researchers reversed the process, those same neuronal responses were much less effective at predicting many of the models' internal features.

This difference was particularly revealing because the researchers did not observe the same problem when comparing neuronal activity across different brains.

Industry observers note that "The results were striking. While AI models can predict the neurons we recorded in the brain fairly well, the brain cannot equally predict many of the model's internal features. Interestingly, this is not the case when neurons from one brain is compared against ones from another brain," says Kar.

The findings suggest that an AI system can produce results that closely resemble those of the brain while relying on very different internal mechanisms. In other words, matching the brain's responses does not necessarily mean that the underlying processes are the same.

Industry observers note that kar warns that this distinction could become increasingly important as artificial intelligence advances. If researchers continue refining models based only on how accurately they predict neural activity, differences between those models and actual primate brains could accumulate over time.

That would undermine one of the main reasons neuroscientists use these systems in the first place: to develop realistic explanations of how the brain works.

"The findings suggest that today's AI systems solve visual tasks partly using internal strategies that the brain may not use. Importantly, the parts of AI models that align with the brain are also better at predicting real human behavior," indicates Kar.

Why the Discovery Matters for Neuroscience and Human Behavior.

The implications extend well beyond computer vision. Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to help researchers design experiments, study human behavior, and investigate neurological and psychological conditions. Many of these applications depend on the assumption that AI models process information in ways that resemble the human brain.

If that assumption is incorrect, researchers could draw misleading conclusions from models that appear accurate on the surface but operate differently underneath.

Recent findings suggest that "Our findings challenge how similar current AI systems really are with the primate brain. We show that models that were previously thought to be brain-like rely on internal components that the brain does not appear to use. We provide a well-vetted diagnostic metric for the field," claims Muzellec.

Developing AI systems that more faithfully reproduce brain function could eventually improve research into conditions ranging from post-traumatic stress disorder to autism. For now, however, the newly identified differences highlight the need for caution when using existing models to investigate human behavior or guide clinical research.

Industry observers note that the concern may also apply to other areas of neuroscience. Similar artificial intelligence models are already being used to study hearing, language, and movement. If those systems also rely on internal processes that differ from biological ones, researchers may need to reconsider how much they can reveal about the nervous system.

Building AI That More Closely Matches the Human Brain.

Rather than suggesting that artificial neural networks should be abandoned, the findings provide a way to make them more useful and scientifically reliable.

By identifying which features of an AI model correspond to real neural activity, researchers can focus on developing systems that more accurately reflect the biological mechanisms behind perception.

"Our approach helps identify which parts of an ANN truly match brain activity, allowing us to build more reliable models for understanding how people see and interpret the world," claims Kar. "This is especially important for our autism research program, which builds on models of the neurotypical brain as a baseline.".

According to recent reports, A neurotypical brain refers to one with patterns of neurological development and functioning generally considered typical. Establishing accurate models of these patterns is important for researchers investigating how perception and information processing may differ in conditions such as autism.

To help other scientists put their findings into practice, the team has released a publicly available testing toolkit that AI developers can use to evaluate their own models and identify opportunities for improvement.

Published in Nature Machine Intelligence, the study introduces a newly introduced approach to evaluating artificial intelligence that goes beyond measuring how well a system performs a task. The researchers argue that understanding whether AI reaches its results through processes that genuinely resemble those of the brain is just as important.

The discovery could help guide the development of a upcoming generation of AI models that not only recognize the world with impressive accuracy, but also offer a more faithful picture of how the human brain makes sense of what it sees.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is chock full of side quests that point you towards bonus hits or gang hideouts.
  • While picking up Jason’s neighbor Shirley’s rum order from a nearby liquor store, you just might hear some squawking the attendant writes off as a loud TV.
  • In a recent development, to start, you’ll want to head to the Three Sheers Liquor store, marked on your map by Shirley when you accept her request to snag her rum order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is chock full of side quests that point you towards bonus hits or gang hideouts. All over Leonida, groups of ner’do wells are making cash and leaving it lying around, all yours for the taking if you’re quick enough on the draw and know where to look.

While picking up Jason’s neighbor Shirley’s rum order from a nearby liquor store, you just might hear some squawking the attendant writes off as a loud TV. In reality, he’s hiding a pretty penny within an exotic animal ring run out the back, and a spiteful parrot is stuck back there ready to spill the beans. Let’s go over the quickest way to find it and run it for all its worth.

In a recent development, to start, you’ll want to head to the Three Sheers Liquor store, marked on your map by Shirley when you accept her request to snag her rum order. Located just down the road from Jason’s place, enter for a small cutscene hinting there's more going on behind closed doors.

Once you secure Shirley’s rum in your trunk, head down the alley to the right of the store. You’ll hear a bunch of people arguing with what sounds like a parrot, insulting the crew and blabbing about hiding cash. Continue down the alley until you spot an opening in the barbed wire cover on the wall.

In a recent development, hop over, and the gang will start a brawl. Be careful, as stepping too far away will prompt multiple members to draw their guns. If you want to get out of this quietly and professionally, make sure you handle the group hand-to-hand; that way, no one calls the cops.

Once you handle all the goons, the parrot will start praising you. By interacting with it, Jason will ask about the money it mentioned, and it will start dropping hints. The notable one is the generator, alluding to the small box generator in the upper left corner of the yard, behind the liquor store.

Sources indicate that go into focus mode, and you’ll notice a small marked crevice in the side of the store, right beside the generator. Interact with it to pocket a cool $1,382, a solid early-game sum that will more than pay for running Shirley’s errands. You can also pocket a number of melee weapons from the goons, including machetes and shovels if you’re looking for a hand-to-hand option.

The liquor store gang is one of many small, unaffiliated criminal groups that you can find throughout Leonida, acting as a great first taste of the kind of rewards that can be hiding right out of plain sight. Return Shirley’s rum, and you’ve had a very successful errand.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heartopia, the upcoming cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a massive launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find fresh outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games notes you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing upcoming inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

It has been revealed that heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

The game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. You should check out how to unlock and upgrade hobbies in Heartopia first, before you get deep into finding all cooking recipes. And, of course, this wouldn’t be a major game launch without a bunch of Heartopia codes for some free stuff.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a new brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on swiftly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

It has been revealed that seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his initiative.

As for the fresh playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Sources indicate that fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

Recent findings suggest that as you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with upcoming special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds latest palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

It has been revealed that marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Britain's Marc 'Caedrel' Lamont and Dan Gaskin were among the winners at the 2026 Esports Awards in Miami, where Counter-Strike 2 was named game of the year and Team Vitality and BLAST also took industry honours. The results crown a strong Counter-Strike year eight days before the next CS2 Major begins in Singapore.

In a recent development, the 2026 Esports Awards honoured two British figures from the streaming and broadcast side of the scene. Caedrel is a League of Legends streamer and co-streamer. Gaskin works as a caster.

The ceremony took place on the evening of 17 November at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County. It is the scene’s main end-of-season awards show. The event began in London in 2016.

At Worlds 2026, Caedrel was the top co-streamer for both hours watched and peak viewers, according to Esports Charts.

It has been revealed that his co-stream success came in a softer year for the tournament overall. Worlds 2026 peaked at 3.98 million viewers, which was 41% lower than the previous year. Caedrel’s numbers show how much attention a single co-streamer can hold even when the event’s headline peak falls.

According to recent reports, gaskin was not the only caster honoured in Miami. The other broadcast honours went to Alex ‘Machine’ Richardson for Play-by-Play Caster of the Year, Iain Chambers for Host of the Year and Anthony ‘NAMELESS’ Wheeler for Analyst of the Year. iShowSpeed was named Streamer of the Year.

Counter-Strike featured prominently among the industry prizes. Vitality’s award as best organisation came alongside Esports PC Player of the Year for Mathieu ‘ZywOo’ Herbaut. OpTic Texas were named Esports Team of the Year.

BLAST, which stages many of its events in Europe, was named Esports Tournament Organiser of the Year.

Vitality’s results through the year back up their award. They beat Spirit to win IEM Rio 2026 on 19 April, giving them back-to-back ESL Grand Slam titles. ZywOo took his 31st career HLTV MVP award at that event.

"When I won this award in 2023, I never thanked my parents" 😅❤️.

Esports Colour Caster of the Year — @DanGaskin pic.twitter.com/oZBw5FItEJ.

— Esports Awards Presented by Thunderpick (@esportsawards) November 18, 2026.

The team’s form held into the autumn. Vitality swept MOUZ 3-0 in the ESL Pro League Season 24 grand final on 11 October. That was their second title in a row after winning StarSeries Fall in September.

Sources indicate that the PGL Major Singapore 2026 runs from 25 November to 13 December with 32 teams and a US$1,250,000 prize pool, The Kallang reported. The final stages will be played at the Singapore Indoor Stadium from 10 to 13 December.

Industry observers note that sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Sources indicate that since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. In a recent development, alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sources indicate that sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has been out for 24-36 hours now, depending on where you live. Players are only just scratching the surface, but they're already making some incredible discoveries in the game's early sections. References to GTA 5's Trevor, Franklin, and Michael have already been spotted, there have been some Dexter Easter eggs, and we could be on our way to the next Mount Chiliad mystery.

Players have also been Googling some very suspect phrases...

The game's simulation mechanics have been taken to the next level this time around, and serious effort has gone into the health and fitness elements. However, while some players like their protagonists buff, others prefer a chunkier, more realistic version.

Within 24 hours, players have min/maxxed their characters' fitness and weight levels, trying to make them as plump as possible. Unfortunately, there are many complaints that the biggest just ain't big enough.

On Reddit, GTA 6 player TheKey32 showed off their max-weight, low-muscle Jason. While there are signs of a double chin emerging, and a bit of a dad bod poking through his shirt, Jason is still buff, and those extra pounds kinda ​​​​​​suit him. There have, naturally, been calls to make him fatter.

The discontent continued throughout the thread, with many pointing to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas' CJ as an example of the heft they'd have liked to see.

In a recent development, while much of the discussion on Reddit focused on Jason, Twitter skewed more towards Lucia. The sentiment, however, remained the same.

I'd argue that max-weight Lucia could just about pass herself off as thicc, but she's not quite at the weight that many were hoping for.

The perceived lack of weight has, in a way, amped up excitement for GTA 6's PC version, with many exclaiming that their first port of call will be to mod the game with XXL protagonists.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside enhancement 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the proposal is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

Sources indicate that the Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

In a recent development, the Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

Recent findings suggest that the Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.

The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be mentioned for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.

According to recent reports, it also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money). So today we're rounding up 20 gems to consider picking up for your trusty Wii.

Recent findings suggest that if you're just looking for the Best Wii Games™, we've got you covered elsewhere. Here, we're specifically looking for games slightly off the beaten track, games that were either full-on exclusives or, in a couple of cases where I've stretched the definition, are difficult to find anywhere else.

Ready? Let's dive right into things...

Kicking things off with the Batman, Wayforward's take on the Cartoon Network series captured perfectly the audio-visual elements of the show with a ton of amusing dialogue and a fun, animated take on a character that — outside of his Lego iteration — had gotten pretty dark and self-serious in the movies and other games of the era.

Batman: The Brave and the Bold - The Videogame (or Das Videospiel as my German copy has it) offers simple side-scrolling brawling, but the BAM-BOOM-POW energy is infectious, and this is a great one to play with the kids. There was a DS version, although that's single-player only, so stick with Wii.

Steven Spielberg's making a game, everybody! Legendary Hollywood director Steven Spielberg! The moment we heard that, we imagined Indiana Jones-style derring-do, or something with aliens or dinosaurs. We didn't imagine that the title prominently flagged as "A Steven Spielberg / EA Game" would be a physics-based block puzzler/party game in the Jenga mould.

Recent findings suggest that however, 2008's Boom Blox turned out to be an absolute blast, especially with friends, and a game that made great use of the system's unique controller. it absolutely deserves to be revisited.

A sequel, Boom Blox Bash Party, followed in 2009, and that's a good time, too.

Dead Space: Extraction was a prequel to the 360-era sci-fi/survival horror game PS3/360 game, and perhaps benefited from low expectations, but it's a cracking, moody little rail shooter.

Sources indicate that this one came to PS3 two years later with Move controller support, but this rail shooter was built for the Wii and made use of one of the system's best features: the IR camera-powered pointer in the Wiimotes. For accuracy and responsiveness, this fairly low-tech solution to pointer controls still trumps the gyro alternative (which constantly needs resetting/recentring) in our book, and this game is worth setting up the sensor bar.

One of the few games Europeans got which never saw the light of day in North America, Disaster: Day of Crisis is a Monolith Soft joint that showcases the Wiimote's versatility with different control schemes across its four main gameplay styles, which naturally includes those video game staples, shooting and driving.

The latter is handled with the Remote held horizontally, while outside the Nunchuk-controlled walking sections, the game becomes a pointer-based rail shooter.

With a blockbusting story that crams in volcanoes alongside shady outfits and plenty of (melo)drama, it doesn't quite cohere as it should, and there are certainly better-looking titles on the system. But as a curio from a studio with an enviable pedigree — and a game that apparently didn't pass Reggie Fils-Aimé's quality bar for release — it's a fascinating glimpse at Monolith's Wii-era thinking before Xenoblade Chronicles dropped two years later.

Excite Truck was an underrated gem in the Wii's early life, with satisfying motion controls that paired beautifully with the wallow-y physics of the arcade monster trucks you raced.

It also let you load up MP3s on your SD card and make your own soundtrack, which felt like a bit of magic to some Wii gamers (read: this Wii gamer) back in 2006. Nothing like boosting over a canyon with Gwen Stefani booming through the speakers. Good times.

Sources indicate that having recently fired up Excite Truck, I can confirm that this holds up beautifully, with subtle controls and a suitable sense of heft and face-blasting speed. Helluva game.

Industry observers note that excitebots, Monster Games' 2009 follow-up, kept the arcade sensibilities and challenging terrain but switched out the trucks for on-wheel robots. It's a fantastic game that injects a little more personality into the basic structure of Excite Truck while keeping the speed and excitement.

Sources indicate that sadly, it's also a game which never launched in Europe, so we're currently tit-for-tat after Disaster: Day of Crisis. North America got the better deal, there.

It has been revealed that look, it's an inconsequential Zelda spin-off designed to showcase the Wii Zapper, but it is a system-exclusive inconsequential Zelda spin-off. Can you afford not to have it in your collection?

Hmm, probably. There's a reason this target-practice game is bottom of our Zelda list. Still, it's not unenjoyable, still dirt cheap, and it's got Twilight Princess-era Link on the box. I've somehow ended up with two copies. One of those 'oh, I don't have this' moments when you get home and realise 'yes, I already have this.'.

Another 'built for Wii' game that came to other platforms later (Vita in 2012, PC in 2016), Cing's Little King's Story added dashes of Doshin The Giant and Pikmin to a real-time strategy tale of the titular diminutive king working to expand the reach of his kingdom one citizen at a time and conquer neighbouring territories,.

An engaging genre mash-up that holds its own alongside the previously mentioned Pikmin series while putting a fresh spin on things, this was one of the last games Cing (Hotel Dusk, Another Code) released. Two years later, the manufacturer filed for bankruptcy.

When PlatinumGames' name is on the box, you expect style - and MadWorld certainly delivered that with its inky, Sin City-esque aesthetic that splattered blood red across a black-and-white canvas.

At a time when all the serious games elsewhere were shiny and brown and grey, this Sega-published chainsaw-'em-up also helped demonstrate that Wii wasn't only a console for fluffy technicolour worlds and cuddly mascots.

As a hack-and-slash brawler, it's not up there with the developer's finest work - there's definitely an element of style over substance here. But when the style is this good, it's still worth the space on the shelf.

Industry observers note that honestly, at this point we all thought we'd have access to this on Switch one way or another — via NSO if not a proper remaster. However, at the time of writing (and discounting the now-unavailable Wii U eShop release of the Trilogy), this Metroid is still a Wii exclusive.

We can only assume it will arrive at some point — Nintendo now has the four Pikmin games on Switch, so it's about time to plug the Prime gap, too.

And staying on that theme, let's stick with Samus over the page...

Feature: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1202 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.
  • I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the latest Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October.
  • Recent findings suggest that some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.

I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the latest Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October. While completing the campaign, I inevitibly came across loads of features that surprised me along the way, so I thought I'd use this opportunity to just highlight a few of them.

Recent findings suggest that some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information. In any case, here are the specific features (avoiding story spoilers) that surprised me as I was completing GTA 6 on Xbox Series X:.

It has been revealed that yeah, there's finally a fuel requirement in a GTA game! It's not too invasive, so don't worry, but if you happen to drive a car around the map for an extensive amount of time, you'll be forced to find a gas station and refuel it (a very short cutscene and a press of the RT button). You can also repair your car at gas stations as well, which certainly comes in handy if you've been smashing it around at high speeds!

You can still break into vehicles the old fashioned way - either stealing it mid-drive or smashing a window to gain access - but you can also use a slim-jim to break the lock, or eventually a key cloner to bypass the security entirely. Be aware of vehicles with trackers though, as if you end up going too slow, the tracker will alert the cops to your location.

It's not always enough to escape the cops and stay hidden from them for an extended period of time. If you really want to ensure you'll lose their attention, you'll want to either ditch the car or take it to a "Pay 'n' Spray" outlet, as well as change your outfit. It's possible to partially do this by throwing on some sunglasses and a hat, but the clever move is to stash one or more outfits in your car's trunk that you can switch between at a moment's notice.

While it's impossible to avoid situations in GTA 6 where you'll be engaging in all sorts of criminal activity, you can handle them in various ways. For example, a mission that requires you to take out a bunch of people can be completed by one-shotting them all, but this will raise your criminal profile. Alternatively, leaving your enemies injured but still alive will push you more towards a "Professional" profile. I haven't properly been able to compare how this affects the game yet (I really need to experiment with both sides of the extreme rather than hovering towards the middle), but Rockstar says it alters how the story, world and Jason / Lucia react to you.

According to recent reports, I always love when games get creative with music - South of Midnight was one that really impressed me - and GTA 6 is now one of the best examples I can think of. Basically, you get highly-curated pumping tunes playing in the background during things like shootouts and getaways, while more menacing situations can feature a different vibe of soundtrack, sometimes even with lyrics. You might not quite understand the appeal until you play it, but it's actually one of my favourite newly introduced features. The use of music in certain cutscenes is awesome as well.

It has been revealed that I don't know if I can verify this yet for sure, but the radio stations either appear to change their music selection based on where you are on the map, or based on how far you've progressed into the story. As I spent more time in Vice City, I started to notice a much bigger range of songs on the Flash FM channel (my favourite) including everyone from Coldplay to The Ting Tings, whereas those tunes never popped up at the start. Try it for yourself and let me know if I'm right about this!

Any GTA game worth its salt has to come with a whole bunch of minigames, and my favourite so far is the addition of minigolf. I believe there are three 18-hole courses dotted around the map in total, and they're beautifully detailed and themed, with genuinely enjoyable holes to play on. There's actual golf as well, but I have to admit I haven't had chance to check it out yet. Pool in the bars is great fun too!

If you really take your time to play through GTA 6, which I highly recommend you do, you'll truly be able to appreciate just how much effort has gone into some of the seemingly smallest aspects of it. Snapmatic, which is the social media platform on your in-game phone, is constantly being updated with latest statuses, photos, videos, comments and more, and you could literally just sit just browsing it for ages and enjoying the interactions. There's also a "News" app that regularly gets updated with fresh articles about what's going on in Leonida.

When you get to a certain mission in GTA 6, you'll be introduced to your first video game inside the game itself, which seems to be a very high-brow parody of modern-day indie hits. There are actually multiple games you can play, including one that's very reminiscent of Xbox title Yet Another Zombie Survivors, and these can either be accessed by turning on your TV or going up to arcade cabinets located in various stores all over the map.

Industry observers note that when GTA 5 came out for Xbox 360 back in 2013, one of the major things I can recall is how slow the initial loading screens would be, especially once GTA Online got involved. We obviously haven't got an online component to GTA 6 just yet, but in terms of loading up the single-player game on Xbox Series X, it's actually a very quick process that isn't painful whatsoever. You barely even notice it!

Of course, these aren't the only surprising features you'll run into while playing GTA 6 - there are literally hundreds and hundreds that are waiting to be discovered. I don't want to spoil anything about the story or the details of the missions themselves though, and ultimately this is a game where surprises will continue being revealed long into the future.

Industry observers note that for now, just go and enjoy it on your Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S (or PS5), and I urge you to take your time and really let it all soak in. One of the perils of reviewing games is that you have to grind to the finish line, and while that does still give you a great impression of the experience, I already can't wait to go back and spend 100+ hours with it this time.

Sources indicate that anything here sound particularly enticing to you? Let us know down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are at the moment working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

According to recent reports, understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s latest ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we strategy for today, tomorrow, and the future.”.

Recent findings suggest that as for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post states that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

It has been revealed that future releases, of course, include newly introduced The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim presently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.).

This obviously isn’t the game’s first collaboration with a known brand, though this one does include a lot of free items and accessories that anyone can make use of, even if they don’t care about Coach.

According to recent reports, the Coach Collection brings nine newly introduced items to The Sims 4. It even included further confirmation, if any was needed, that Project Rene is a dedicated mobile off-shoot, and not — as many had long believed — The Sims 5.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most hotly anticipated games of all time, and few things can slow down its momentum, thanks to the sheer hype and quality on display.
  • Recent findings suggest that the streets of Leonida have been plagued by a number of minor graphical and physics bugs that have led to laughs, but one repeat offender is causing issues for PS5 players.
  • It has been revealed that for a massive open-world story game like Grand Theft Auto 6, forced short playtimes can be a killer, and the constant crashes forced by error code CE-108255-1 are causing just that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most hotly anticipated games of all time, and few things can slow down its momentum, thanks to the sheer hype and quality on display. The quickest thing to put a damper on excitement, sadly, is bugs, hiccups that are both unintended and hard to fix in any quick manner.

Recent findings suggest that the streets of Leonida have been plagued by a number of minor graphical and physics bugs that have led to laughs, but one repeat offender is causing issues for PS5 players. Internally titled error code CE-108255-1, this bug causes a no-frills, hard crash back to the PlayStation home screen after a brief play window, causing players to lose progress and time as they’re forced to reset.

It has been revealed that for a massive open-world story game like Grand Theft Auto 6, forced short playtimes can be a killer, and the constant crashes forced by error code CE-108255-1 are causing just that. Complaints across the internet say the error has no discernible cause, but it only appears on PlayStation 5 systems, leaving Xbox players in the clear.

A recent set of firmware updates could be causing the error afflicting PS5 players, but neither Sony nor Rockstar has released any statement on it. Hopefully, as more players stumble into it, a swift hotfix patches the issue before too many lose potentially hours of playtime to a simple bug. GTA6’s robust simulation elements would make the loss even harder, taking tons of hard work with it.

Sources indicate that no usual methods seem to help; reinstalling the game, going offline, and keeping the system cool all seem to be fruitless. Without a proper fix, players are stuck just hoping it doesn’t happen to them, a frustrating possibility that could easily tarnish their experience playing such an anticipated release.

The quickest thing to put a damper on excitement, sadly, is bugs, hiccups that are both unintended and hard to fix in any quick manner.

Across the board, Grand Theft Auto 6 seems very well optimized, despite being trapped at 30 FPS across all platforms. A frame unlock is likely to come with the PC version, either officially or thanks to mods once the title jumps ship from consoles. Until then, fans are forced to pray and keep playing, crossing their fingers that their hard-earned cash isn’t lost due to the whims of an error they can’t avoid.

Over the last decade or so, a number of massive AAA titles have been released frankly unfinished. With Cyberpunk 2077 as the biggest offender, players have gotten sick and tired of being forced to shuffle through mountains of bugs and errors in order to play the games they pay for.

That makes Grand Theft Auto 6’s error code CE-108255-1 all the more frustrating; with how well polished the vast majority of the experience is, a hiccup like this sticks out like a sore thumb. The fine folks at Rockstar have clearly spent over a decade of blood, sweat, and tears to make Grand Theft Auto 6 the powerhouse it is, and losing face because of a bug like this is just sad.

With no acknowledgement from the studio yet, fans are left to their own devices, and some have gotten more than a little spiteful.

No physical copy, a $79.99 base price tag, and multiple on-disc locations barred behind a special edition give GTA6 an outer coat that has nothing to do with its criminal focus. It feels like the industry is yet again at a tipping point set by a big player, with the future in the hands of the rest of the AAA developers surrounding them.

  • According to recent reports, season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off.
  • In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios mentioned that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The right now ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

According to recent reports, season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios mentioned that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something newly introduced in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Industry observers note that escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj.

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Industry observers note that similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several upcoming customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

Update [Wed 18th Nov 2026, 3:19pm]: Digital Foundry has also shared an analysis of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X|S today, and you can watch their video at the bottom of this article. We've covered it in more depth elsewhere on Pure Xbox too:.

Original Story: With GTA 6 reviews now out in the wild, and countless Xbox players already getting access to it via the controversial Fresh Zealand trick, it's no surprise that we've also got loads of screenshots and clips doing the rounds online.

One of the best sources for raw Xbox gameplay footage is the YouTube channel Fuzion Xbox Testing, and they're already uploaded their initial look at both the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S versions of GTA 6.

On Xbox Series X, it's very much what you'd expect - a really amazing-looking game with an internal resolution of 1440p, upscaled to 4K. The 30FPS performance is largely smooth, but does drop frames on occasion.

I also played GTA 6 on Xbox Series X for our Pure Xbox review, and here's what I said about it:.

"Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well...".

"It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably big frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences.".

In a recent development, on Xbox Series S, GTA 6 still looks really impressive from a visual standpoint, even though some drawbacks have clearly been made in terms of ray tracing and texture quality. The frame rate in the game's initial opening is shown to be a locked 30FPS in some sequences, dropping into the mid-20s during busier moments.

It has been revealed that overall though, the feedback we've seen from Xbox Series S players thus far has been very positive, especially in terms of how impressive the game looks. Rockstar Games actually talked to Wccftech about the Series S version as well, revealing they're using AMD FSR Upscaling 4 to scale the resolution to 1080p.

"On the Xbox Series S, we’re starting from a base resolution of 720p, which is scaled to 1080p using AMD FSR Upscaling 4.".

Recent findings suggest that "...[our] focus on lighting made it vital for us to ensure we could use the same lighting solution on each console, including the Xbox Series S, where memory pressure posed a bit of a challenge. The results made that a challenge worth overcoming.".

Industry observers note that great stuff, then! We'll leave you with the comparison footage for GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S down below.

Are you playing on either console yet? What do you think of the visuals and performance? Tell us in the comments.

In a recent development, however, the Team of the Year selection hasn’t been without controversy. The FC 26 TOTY promo is voted for by players, you probably cast your vote by selecting time-limited gold cards yourself, but that method has led some to question whether the Team of the Year is more of a popularity contest than a true measure of performance. This is with specific reference to Virgil, whose in-and-out form during Liverpool’s poor start this season has caused some to question his eight-straight inclusion.

In yet another blow to those of us who got Mario Gomez and Gianluca Vialli from the Classic XI Hero pack, during the TOTY event these Classic XI Heroes will be further upgraded to TOTY Honorable Mentions Heroes.

More TOTY items will also be dropping over the next couple of weeks, including a men’s and women’s 12th player, Honorable Mentions, 2 teams of TOTY Icons and both a men’s and women’s “Captain of the Year”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that what a stupendous launch for GTA 6, right? The game just became one of the highest-grossing entertainment pieces in the entire industry, and not only are the sales high, but the game is just full of a ton of insane details, mechanics and easter eggs to gush about, especially if you’re a hardcore fan like me.

Speaking of fanboying, if you're a fan of cheesy Hollywood blockbusters, you may have enjoyed the original Fast and Furious movies. If so, I have a surprise for you. The madmen at Rockstar have added Brian’s (Paul Walker) Eclipse to GTA 6 as an Easter Egg, and it is an absolute thing of beauty.

So, if you want to know more about where you can quickly find this car and own it for yourself, then join me for this brief guide for GTA 6, where I’ll discuss the location of the iconic green Eclipse from the first Fast and Furious movie, as well as how you can own it.

Note: I strongly recommend being in Chapter 2 when you try to get this car; you’ll see why.

According to recent reports, more specifically, this is a modified Penumbra, which looks almost identical to the iconic '95 Eclipse from the Fast and Furious franchise. You can find this specialized car at the dead center of Vespucci Islands, located in the heart of Vice City.

According to recent reports, the location is shown above, so make your way over; the exact spot is a house with a locked fence gate you can climb over. Either just open the garage or go through the side door to find the modified Penumbra with the unique livery.

Recent findings suggest that and much like the buster that got Dom out of handcuffs in the movie, you’ll have to break open and hotwire the car to steal it for yourself here. It will set off an alarm that will alert nearby residents and eventually the cops, so I strongly advise you to get the car out of there immediately.

Industry observers note that of course, if you’re in Chapter 1, you won’t have an option to own or register another car as Jason. However, once you make it to Chapter 2, you can register a car with Lucia after you first visit a guy named Moses at a garage. This is where I strongly recommend you get this car because the first one you register with Moses is free of charge, as long as the car you bring is low-key.

The Green ’95 Eclipse Penumbra will work without any challenges, so you can bring it straight back to his garage and get this beauty owned under Lucia. But there’s a slight catch that may rub you the wrong way.

Recent findings suggest that registering this car as your first free one from Moses means you have to wipe the livery off and replace it with a standard paint job. Don’t panic; it may look like you can’t recover the iconic livery, but you actually can: just visit the Vice Vinyl Mod shop in Vice City, and this garage should give you the option to restore the car's original livery/paint job.

The latest Japanese charts data is in, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has comfortably maintained its lead with another 86,097 sales. Next in line is Metaphor: ReFantazio as its hits the Switch 2, shifting a total of 11,167 units.

Recent findings suggest that pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy also made its debut, selling just 2,854 copies to land at number 9. Now, it's important to note that many owners of the game on Switch 1 will have simply bought the upgrade pack, which won't count toward this total, however the game has also seen its fair share of controversy soon after release.

It has been revealed that it current holds a user score of 6.4 over on Metacritic, though this was as low as 2.3 just the other day as players reported their disappointment at the lack of brand-fresh content, no 60fps support, and supposedly longer load times. Indeed, we gave it a score of 7/10 in our review – a relatively low verdict for such a consistently strong series – citing the lack of seemingly obvious features like mouse mode and higher frame rate.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events.
  • Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.
  • According to recent reports, there’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

According to recent reports, there’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Industry observers note that speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a latest Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of fresh careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

According to recent reports, the aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing newly introduced free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free enhancement, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

  • Recent findings suggest that epic Games quickly caught wind of what players were doing and, earlier this morning, disabled geysers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that fortnite players are coming up with some incredibly inventive ways to make the Pirate Shop Access grind a little easier. Endlessly opening chests gets tedious, fast, and the community wants to scratch off as many lottery tickets as it can.

One pretty busted way of doing that was ramming an SUV into a geyser and jumping out to infinitely glide, essentially giving players flight. That might not sound useful, but you could fly into and destroy entire buildings, opening hundreds of chests in minutes.

Recent findings suggest that epic Games quickly caught wind of what players were doing and, earlier this morning, disabled geysers. Considering the next Treasure Hours is today, with boosted token odds, it's no wonder the team worked so quickly to shut this one down.

Sources indicate that this comes just days after the Respawn Rumble exploit. For whatever reason, rewards — including the Pirate Shop Access tokens — were enabled, and it was clear this was unintentional because they popped up with greyed-out chest icons and the name, 'PH' (placeholder).

It has been revealed that since you would respawn infinitely in Respawn Rumble, players took advantage of this open window to rush the storm and open however many chests they could. Later that day, Epic rolled out a fix.

Don't get the RNG twisted, though. Opening 137,500 chests doesn't guarantee you a token. There's a 0.00073% chance of finding the Pirate Shop Access, and the odds reset on every single chest. The reason players are finding inventive ways to open as many chests as possible is simply to roll the dice more, but your odds are in the toilet no matter how many you open.

Still, as far as Pirate Shop Access grinds go, flying like Superman into every building, boat, and pirate cove is one of the more creative.

In a recent development, if you haven't given up and moved onto GTA 6 yet, the next Treasure Hours window is later today at 11am PT (7pm GMT), with 1.5x boosted odds (meaning you have a 1 in 91,667 chance of finding a token, or a 0.00109% chance). You won't be able to open 500 chests in minutes with the SUV-geyser trick, but if you come back at 6pm PT (2am GMT), the odds will be doubled.

Three Substantial Takeaways From Digital Foundry's GTA 6 Analysis For Xbox Series X|S

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The good folks over at Digital Foundry have been sharing their deep dive analysis on the Xbox Series X|S versions of GTA 6 today, presented in the form of a 23-minute video on YouTube, and a separate article over on their website.
  • Looking at both of these, there's a ton of interesting information that's shared about the two Xbox versions of the game, so we thought we'd provide a quick summary of what they think about GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S.
  • This is just a summary though, and there's way more context and detail in the video at the bottom of this article.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The good folks over at Digital Foundry have been sharing their deep dive analysis on the Xbox Series X|S versions of GTA 6 today, presented in the form of a 23-minute video on YouTube, and a separate article over on their website.

Looking at both of these, there's a ton of interesting information that's shared about the two Xbox versions of the game, so we thought we'd provide a quick summary of what they think about GTA 6 on Xbox Series X and S.

This is just a summary though, and there's way more context and detail in the video at the bottom of this article.

Digital Foundry reckons that the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 is a great-looking game for the most part, highlighting things like lighting, reflections and even the incredible hair system, while also pointing out minor downsides such as missing shadows and occasionally blurry appearances. They also reckon that the frame rate generally maintains its 30FPS target, but will slip in busy situations like chases and explosions.

Recent findings suggest that "Generally speaking, the game acquits itself quite well on Microsoft's senior current-gen console. Visual settings seem pretty solid across the board.".

In a recent development, the Xbox Series S version is also noted to be pretty good in the graphical department, retaining the core features that make GTA 6 such a great game visually. It's the frame rate that bothers DF the most, as it's much more variable and prone to falling below its 30FPS target. That said, it appears to hover around 25-30FPS for the most part.

"Series S offers the loosest 30fps lock, with large portions of the game playing out at frame-rates from the mid to high 20s. Again, it's possible to depress the frame-rate to around 20fps with vehicular destruction. The other consoles do a credible job of hitting 30fps, but Series S often lies in a 25-30fps no-man's-land.".

It has been revealed that if you're wondering which console is the absolute best to play GTA 6 on, it's unsurprisingly the PS5 Pro. Nevertheless, Digital Foundry says that both the Xbox Series X and the PS5 versions "look and play well" despite their softer image (and the Series X is actually "slightly smoother" when setting the Xbox to 120Hz with a VRR display), while the Xbox Series S version is the "hardest to recommend" despite its surprisingly impressive visuals.

"In terms of visual features and performance, the PS5 Pro version is the best option available, with solid frame-rates, 4K-like image quality and a noticeable visual upgrade thanks to ray-traced shadows. However, the game looks and plays well on base PS5 and Xbox Series X as well, despite occasional minor frame-rate drops during regular play and a softer 1440p image. The Series S version of the game is the hardest to recommend, with consistent frame-rate drops to the mid-20s, a 1080p output resolution and a long list of visual cutbacks, though the overall character of the game's visuals still shines through.".

Both the video and the website article are totally different from each other, so it's worth watching / reading the pair of them and getting a better idea of how GTA 6 fares across both Xbox consoles (and PS5 for that matter).

In my experience, I've found GTA 6 to be fantastic on Xbox Series X across the board for the most part, and while the Series S version is clearly a little more unstable, I'd wager that most players will still be perfectly happy with it.

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

8 Best Ways to Build Lucia and Jason’s Relationship in GTA 6

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1115 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has two main protagonists.
  • They don’t automatically start off being thicker than thieves.
  • You have to make sure to care about your partner, and not just treat them as any other character in the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has two main protagonists. They are Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and the pair are madly in love with one another. At least, you are going to want them to be. They have a chance to be more like friends by the end of the story.

They don’t automatically start off being thicker than thieves. Instead, they have a budding relationship that you must help develop, and there are multiple ways that you can help it grow and flourish throughout the game.

You have to make sure to care about your partner, and not just treat them as any other character in the game. Do you think you can do that?

Recent findings suggest that when you start up Grand Theft Auto 6, you play as Jason for a while. You don’t actually start playing as Lucia until the second chapter of the game. This is mostly because the first chapter is dedicated to her getting out of prison and adjusting to life outside.

When you get the call that she is getting out of prison soon, you need to start prepping the house if you want her to be happy. This means that you will want to fix the roof, outside steps, and the wall in the bedroom.

Each of these will help Lucia feel more at home and make her more happy when she gets out of prison, and it will give a serious boost to the relationship.

Your partner will drop hints in dialogue about things they expect you to do. For instance, Lucia and Jason will go to a bar shortly after she gets out of prison. During this time, she will ask Jason to grab her another drink.

If you don’t grab her a drink, it will be brought up in the next conversation, and it will ultimately decrease your relationship score because you didn’t listen to what she asked of you.

You need to pay attention to what your partner says, and if they ask you to do something, it is important that you go out of your way to do it so they don’t get upset.

Sources indicate that early in the game, you need to set yourself up a BuckMe account. It is this game’s version of Venmo or PayPal, which allows you to send and receive money. It also lets you save money, and that is the key.

It has been revealed that as part of the story, Lucia and Jason are saving up money for their family. This means that they need to put money aside for the future. This will also help them open a real bank account.

Whenever you are able to, put money aside so that you can put it towards your future, as this will make your partner very happy. It reveals you are being responsible.

A massive part of any relationship is showing your partner that you care and that you are there for them, and you can do this in multiple ways, but one way is physical affection. This can take many forms, even the simple holding of a hand.

Whenever Jason and Lucia are together, they have the option to hold hands. You will see the option to hold your partner’s hand in the bottom right corner of the screen. When this appears, it is good to pay attention to it.

Sources indicate that holding hands in public shows your partner you are there with them and lets them know they can count on you. It’s a simple but important gesture.

In a recent development, another means of showing your partner that you care is purchasing them gifts. Everyone loves to get a gift, as it shows that they are being thought about, and the same applies for both Lucia and Jason in GTA 6.

There are various opportunities for you to purchase gifts for your partner. For instance, Jason can purchase a necklace for Lucia at the start of the game before she gets out of prison.

Sources indicate that gifts don’t have to be lavish. Instead, you can simply think about what your partner is going to eat. Go out to the store and grab a couple of food items for them and they will definitely be happy about it.

It should go without saying that your partner should be the one you think of first when doing activities, but it might need to be spelled out for some people. Throughout the game, you have the opportunity to put the needs of your partner first or do other activities.

Recent findings suggest that if you choose to do something else, they will be upset and you will lose points in your relationship. For instance, there is a time when Lucia will want Jason to talk to Mattia.

According to recent reports, if you choose to do other things first, like hang out with Cal, Lucia will be noticeably upset with Jason that he chose to do something else before the thing she asked him to do. Putting your partner first will increase your relationship score promptly.

According to recent reports, after a while, you will have full access to Vice City and the glorious sun-baked land of Leonida. That means that you have plenty of activities you can take part in. At this point in the game, you will be playing the game mostly as a duo, which means you can take part in activities together.

Recent findings suggest that there are games that can be played like mini-golf, and then there’s other stuff like kayaking that you can do. These are all considered dates, and they are key to take part in, as they will immensely help your relationship.

As part of the dating mechanic, your partner will mention things they are interested in doing, and taking part in these activities will increase your bond, so make sure you pay attention to what they say while you are out and about.
