Industry observers note that fnatic has confirmed the departure of its longest-serving player, jungler Razork, who is set to join Team Heretics. With support Lospa also set to leave, the London club faces a near-total LEC roster rebuild for 2027.

Fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027. Razork was the London club’s longest-serving player and its main playmaker. He leaves after five seasons in the jungle.

Sources indicate that the club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition. He had entered the LEC with Misfits Gaming in 2020 before moving to Fnatic in 2022. The club later extended his contract to run through 2026.

According to recent reports, his next stop appears to be Team Heretics. Sheep Esports reported that the 26-year-old will play alongside midlaner Jackies and support Jun. Heretics had already tried to sign him a year earlier. On that occasion it agreed a buyout with Fnatic but could not agree terms with the player.

The rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

That deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

Industry observers note that the overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

In a recent development, for the UK scene, the scale of change matters. Fnatic is one of the LEC’s best-supported clubs among British fans.

The club has also opened a search for a League of Legends General Manager. Its job advert says Fnatic goes into a rebuild in 2027. The latest hire will run recruitment of players, coaches and staff, including transfers and benchings, and will manage the team’s budget.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has already outgrossed the entire box office run of Avengers: Endgame, the highest-grossing movie in history — and the sheer scale of that success is represented in the launch day stats.

According to Mat Piscatella, senior director and video game industry advisor at Circana, over 50% of all active consoler customers played GTA 6 at launch, averaging 494–513 minutes of playtime, or roughly 8 hours.

That does not mean 50% of all console users played it.

"For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6," he posted to Bluesky. "PS5 GTA 6 players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494. Both the DAU and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers.".

Piscatella doesn't have the exact stats to hand, explaining that it's "not exactly easy to go back and sort daily active engagement rates," but to his recollection, during his time at Circana, there has been "nothing near this.".

According to recent reports, the only game second to GTA 6 on launch was Fortnite, accounting for 10% of all active players across both platforms. Clearly, the Pirate Shop Access tokens are working.

As for what GTA 6 players were up to before the game debuted, Piscatella had some additional stats, sharing the top-five games between November 6 and 19:.

$3.7 billion in revenue within 24 hours, "the biggest entertainment launch of all time," accounting for over 50% of all active console users — those numbers are nothing to scoff at.

In fact, in less than a week, with 32.5 million copies sold, GTA 6 is already one of the best-selling games of all-time. It right now sits on the edge of the top 30 after overtaking Super Mario Odyssey, Borderlands 2, and Monster Hunter: World.

Considering that GTA 5 is the third best-selling game of all-time, behind only Minecraft and Tetris (clearly, the secret to selling hundreds of millions of copies is blocks), it's easy to imagine GTA 6 landing somewhere near the top.

  • Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending enhancement has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Sources indicate that patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller upgrade. When Battlefield Studios revealed it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

Recent findings suggest that the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

Recent findings suggest that the end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

Recent findings suggest that the other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

Sources indicate that and, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Recent findings suggest that finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, fresh reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was promptly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance Upcoming Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

Sources indicate that however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Fresh Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-latest globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no unveiled platforms.

Sources indicate that although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

[Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

The one that catches the eye is Vice: Magic City Mayhem, which we mentioned recently in our article about two Vice City games releasing in mid-November. While the cover art is very GTA-inspired, and it's set in a world with a "Vice City theme", it actually appears to have more in common with classic Zelda in terms of the gameplay style.

It's also a very temporary Xbox and and Epic Games Store exclusive, as the Steam, PS5 and Nintendo Switch versions have been slightly delayed for whatever reason.

Beyond this, three games are being added to the Xbox Game Pass Premium service today, with High on Life 2 arguably being the highlight (if you enjoy the kind of humour it throws at you). The other two are Call of the Elder Gods and Roadside Research, which are both worth a play as well.

GTA 6 is technically already out in some countries as well (such as Fresh Zealand), but its official release date is November 19th rather than the 18th, so we'll highlight it in tomorrow's article instead.

We'll throw all of today's latest Xbox releases and Xbox Game Pass additions down below.

Vice: Magic City Mayhem is a top-down 8-bit retro action/adventure game inspired by Zelda with a Vice City theme. Step into the shoes of Dutch, one of Magic City’s most feared enforcers, on a thrilling and dangerous quest to rescue your one true love, Sophie. Navigate through the chaos of wild nightclubs, scenic beaches, and raptor-infested yachts in this raunchy, high-stakes adventure.

Industry observers note that turn-based management roguelike. Command the Inquisition and rule an industrial city on the empire’s edge. Use your train to meet prisoner shipment quotas by hunting heretics and slaying magical beasts. Produce supplies, contain revolt, and sacrifice prisoners to stop the madness.

Industry observers note that an intergalactic conspiracy threatens the fate of humanity! Team up with a wide cast of talking alien guns as you shoot, stab, and skate your way through the exotic locales to take down the bad guys and save your favorite species (humans)!

Journey to the far corners of the Earth and unearth ancient horrors in this Lovecraftian narrative puzzle adventure and sequel to 2020’s critically acclaimed Call of the Sea.

In a recent development, roadside Research is a 1 to 4 player co-op gas station simulator. Except you’re aliens. And undercover. Do very human things like restocking shelves while preparing for the invasion. Just don’t get caught.

GTA VI: Best Places to Find Planes

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that planes are, without a doubt, the fastest way to get around the map in GTA VI.
  • However, finding a plane is easier remarked than done.
  • If you are looking for a sweet plane to take up into the skies, you have come to the right place.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that planes are, without a doubt, the fastest way to get around the map in GTA VI. They can help you explore areas to find points of interest or simply get to a pinged location in a flash.

However, finding a plane is easier remarked than done. In GTA VI, planes are typically found in very specific locations such as airports and airstrips.

If you are looking for a sweet plane to take up into the skies, you have come to the right place. Here are the best places to get a plane in Grand Theft Auto VI.

Players can find an airstrip on the southeast side of the Grassrivers in Mariana County. This airstrip has a plane that’s easy to control, and there is usually no one around, making it easy to steal.

In a recent development, in the northern section of Belville in Leonard County, you will find Lake Leonida. Next to one of the docks on the lake, you will find a plane that’s easy to steal because the open water acts as a runway and there aren’t many people around.

In Borrachero Sound, a very small area on the west side of Kelly County, you will find an airstrip that lies next to the water. You'll usually find more than one plane here, so you’ll have options to choose from.

In the Waning Sands region of Leonard County, you will find an airstrip just outside of Belville. Similar to the plane spot mentioned earlier, you will also find more than one plane at this airstrip.

Recent findings suggest that last, but certainly not least, one of the best places to find a plane is, of course, the Vice City International Airport. Known as VCIA, you can find this airport in the southwest section of Vice Dale County.

Keep in mind that VCIA has high security, so stealing a plane can be tricky. However, it is an airport, so it has the most planes available, making it one of the best places to find one.

If you’d like to get a plane in a more natural way, that doesn’t involve stealing, you can find one during the McKittrick Farm side quest. To start this quest, examine the poster inside the Starlet Motel office (mandatory location in Chapter 2), and the location of the farm will be marked on your map.

Since you’ll be stealing the planes mentioned in this guide, it’s wise to learn how to avoid the cops when flying. Even though the places I mentioned here tend to have almost no one around, with the exception of VCIA, there’s still a possibility that someone will spot you stealing it or report the crime once they realize it's missing.

The best way to avoid cops' detection when flying a plane is to fly at low altitude. Flying low makes it harder for cops to see you, as buildings, trees, and other structures will help block their line of sight.

Recent findings suggest that you only really need to worry about this if the heat star level reaches 3 to 4, when police bring in the helicopters. Otherwise, you can easily lose cops by simply flying away due to how fast planes go in the game.

GTA 6 On Switch 2? Digital Foundry Weighs In On The Possibility

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (395 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Could Grand Theft Auto 6 come to Switch 2?
  • In the outlet's latest rundown, it touches on the "compromised" Xbox Series S performance.
  • However, the experts point out that a Switch 2 port "feels extremely unlikely at this stage".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Could Grand Theft Auto 6 come to Switch 2? That has been the major question ever since Nintendo officially revealed its console last year, and it's something that we have mused over ever since (as unlikely as it may seem at an initial glance). Now that the game is out, the tech experts over at Digital Foundry have weighed in on the port possibility, and, perhaps unsurprisingly, they don't rate its chances.

In the outlet's latest rundown, it touches on the "compromised" Xbox Series S performance. It isn't all that, with DF noting "frame-rates routinely lingering in the mid to high 20s during ordinary traversal and combat," but it's the system that regularly lands the most comparisons to Switch 2, so DF says that it would be "interesting" to see if it would be "possible for a further cut back version to ship on Nintendo's hybrid console".

However, the experts point out that a Switch 2 port "feels extremely unlikely at this stage".

"Unless there are massive changes made," DF's John Linneman states around the 53:24 mark in the above video, "I don't see how this could possibly work on Switch 2".

The main reasoning seems to mostly come down to the sheer size of the damn thing. This is a game that is pushing even the highest-end consoles to their limit — "the huge CPU burden that restricts GTA 6 to 30fps on even PS5 Pro" — so how would the comparatively little guy Switch 2 ever stand a chance?

Recent findings suggest that now, we're never willing to rule anything out completely. Switch 1 got its fair share of 'impossible ports' in its lifetime, and Switch 2 has already landed a handful of beefy boys that we previously never could have imagined making the jump intact. However, this one might be a step too far. Please do prove us wrong, Rockstar!

Sources indicate that it's a shame, because by all accounts, the game is fantastic. Our sister sites Push Square and Pure Xbox both gave it 10/10 reviews, praising it as one of the greatest open worlds of all time. It shot right to the top of Metacritic's ratings, too, tying with Ocarina of Time as the best of the best.

Do you think we'll one day see GTA 6 on Switch 2? Let us know in the comments.

Battlefield 6’s first substantial map in months is coming to Labs soon, but I'm more excited about BF4's Golmud Railway making its way to BF6

📅 23 Jan 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content.
  • As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content.
  • The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the fresh maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a major component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the fresh maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

It has been revealed that the blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of substantial maps as Battlefield 6 at the moment is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

Sources indicate that more Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off latest gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios stated we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

It has been revealed that ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

For context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its concerns elsewhere, and BF Studios notes it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

It has been revealed that finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

It has been revealed that redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

#63591. Latest Update: GTA 6 Lets You Stop And Even Derail The Train

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: GTA 6 Lets You Stop And Even Derail The Train

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (415 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it might've been impossible, but for 13 years, that didn't stop GTA 5 players from throwing everything they could at the freight train to try and stop it dead in its tracks.
  • Not only can you stop the train in GTA 6, but you can even derail it.
  • Trains are much more dynamic this time around, reacting to their environment rather than pushing on full steam ahead without any thought to what's in front of them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it might've been impossible, but for 13 years, that didn't stop GTA 5 players from throwing everything they could at the freight train to try and stop it dead in its tracks. What began with ramming a dump truck into it quickly spiraled into spawning 100 rhino tanks, placing a UFO on the tracks, or even flooding Los Santos with a tsunami. Nothing worked. So, when GTA 6 finally hit store shelves, the number one question people raced to answer was: can you stop the train?

Not only can you stop the train in GTA 6, but you can even derail it. As shown by Twitter user jax_caine (video embedded below), the train isn't an unstoppable force of nature anymore. Hitting it from the side causes it to swerve off the rails, and if you wait around for another train, the two will collide.

Trains are much more dynamic this time around, reacting to their environment rather than pushing on full steam ahead without any thought to what's in front of them.

In a recent development, if you stand on the tracks, a train will brake before hitting you. Likewise, when the train sees another train blocking the tracks, rather than ramming into it at full speed and causing a massive pile-up, it'll slow down. Hell, if you put a body on the tracks, they stop and even sound their horn at you.

Sources indicate that GTA 5's trains worked a little differently. They're static objects and their position is updated through coordinates, independent of physics interactions, which means that instead of reacting to the game's physics engine, they follow hard-coded tracks and override anything in their way. That's why they turn into submersibles when you flood Los Santos, and easily tear through 100 tanks. They literally can't be stopped.

We don't know exactly how they work in GTA 6 yet, but it's clear they aren't static objects anymore. They behave like other vehicles, reacting dynamically to the world. You could fly a plane into the train and it'd be thrown off course, rather than bravely continuing ahead without a scratch.

Still, even with GTA 6 in hand and a train that we can derail, I doubt that'll stop the community from finding increasingly elaborate ways to stop the freight train. Even if they never do. With that mystery out of the way, maybe we can turn our attention to those strange symbols near Manifest Canyon, eh?

10 Game Boy Metroidvanias You Can Finish in Under 10 Hours

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1057 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that for a long time, Metroidvanias have been a bit of an oddball when compared to some other games.
  • Very few games ever even attempted to push the envelope of Metroidvanias aside from those that coined the term, Metroid and Castlevania.
  • The Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance could see players complete the game in one long car ride, provided it wasn’t too dark outside just yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for a long time, Metroidvanias have been a bit of an oddball when compared to some other games. They’re still great games, sometimes the best titles of a console generation, but back in the day they were more niche.

Very few games ever even attempted to push the envelope of Metroidvanias aside from those that coined the term, Metroid and Castlevania. One of the biggest draws of these games is that you could complete them pretty quickly, especially when it came to the handheld consoles.

The Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance could see players complete the game in one long car ride, provided it wasn’t too dark outside just yet. This list encompasses the shortest Metroidvanias of the broader Game Boy generation that you could finish in under ten hours.

Industry observers note that starting off with a strange one that fits a bit more into a Metroidvania-like category, Wario Land 3 did incorporate a lot of aspects of Metroidvanias. Playing as the treasure-obsessed Wario, players would navigate various levels attempting to find all the treasure chests available.

Recent findings suggest that in true Metroidvania fashion, players could return to older levels of the game with newly introduced abilities to uncover other secrets they couldn’t get to before. The game did manage to make a name for itself thanks to some innovative gameplay elements and its relatively quick run-through.

Now the Castlevania series is absolutely a true Metroidvania, and one of the more difficult by many people's standards. Playing as Nathan Graves, players will enter Dracula’s Castle in an attempt to rescue their mentor.

According to recent reports, while not part of the main continuity of Castlevania, the game gained a following thanks to the difficulty and use of the Dual Set-Up System. This system gave players the ability to create new combinations of attacks via a card-collecting system, for interesting results.

According to recent reports, many of the best Castlevania games incorporate some sort of gimmick to make them a bit more interesting, and Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is no exception. Fifty years before Simon Belmont took on Dracula, there was Juste Belmont and their journey through Dracula’s Castle.

The main feature of the game was the two versions of Dracula’s Castle that saw players moving between the two to solve mysteries and unlock paths intertwined between them. That’s probably the reason the game is on the longer side compared to most of the other Metroidvanias of the time.

In a recent development, in a surprising twist, this Castlevania game is actually set in the future, in 2035. It also abandoned the Belmonts for a brand new protagonist, Soma Cruz, who would discover his strange ability after being drawn to the castle during an eclipse.

In keeping with the lore of the game, the major system here was called the Tactical Soul System, and it would allow Soma to gain new abilities based on the soul he collected. This drove the main idea behind the Metroidvania aspects of the game and granted some freedom in character builds that players enjoyed.

Whether you’ve heard of the series or seen something from it, almost everyone can recognize Shantae for one reason or another. The series introduced in 2002 with some great Metroidvania elements that gained a large following, making it fairly popular.

Sources indicate that the game introduced players to the half-genie protagonist Shantae as she did battle against her arch-nemesis Risky Boots. The key feature of the game was that Shantae could dance to transform herself into animals to perform different tasks and movement challenges, accessing other areas.

It has been revealed that the first Metroid game on the list, but not the first to pioneer the series, Metroid Fusion was the fourth game in the series. It brought a different kind of focus to the series, with the game sticking more to narrative and suspense than previous installments.

In a recent development, this proved to be a great idea as the game revolved around Samus Aran and the infamous SA-X, a duplicate made with an infected suit. It brought an air of suspense to the game that stuck with players despite how short the game was.

Unlike some of the other Metroid games, Metroid: Zero Mission sought to update the original game for a more modern era. Zero Mission introduced a lot of quality-of-life features to make the age of the original game a bit more manageable.

The game took pieces from previous titles that it had learned from, incorporating more story and expanded content. While still short, Metroid: Zero Mission managed to set a newly introduced path for the Metroid series as a whole, and is still seen as one of its highlights.

The second game in the series, Metroid II: Return of Samus, is one of the most iconic of all. This title introduced a few of the most memorable features that would become staples of the series, like the Spider Ball.

Industry observers note that not only did the game introduce some new mechanics, but it also focused on a darker world and story for the Metroidvania. The game clearly helped to build a dedicated fanbase despite its shortness, as its influences can be seen even in the newer Metroid releases today.

A Metroidvania before the genre was even established, TMNT III: Radical Rescue was arguably one of the first few Metroidvanias. It featured a story focused on rescuing the turtles from the claws of Shredder in a beat-em-up exploration-focused game.

Each of the four turtles had a special use that would unlock more of the map for you to explore, effectively making the game a great Metroidvania-style game. There’s certainly an argument to be made that it would go on to inspire features in the genre.

A controversial title that ended up being basically expelled from the series for narrative reasons. It was a bit different from other entries in the series, being a more stage-based game rather than focusing on traditional navigation.

Regardless of any of that, the game is the shortest Metroidvania from the Game Boy era, clocking in at around two hours total. While perhaps not the most key Metroidvania over the years, it certainly has its place in history and our hearts. What a little curio.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously unveiled demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically rolled out first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that it is laying off a total of 166 members of staff from its Canadian offices.

The teams affected, Ubisoft Montréal and Ubisoft Québec, are arguably two of the most prominent studios in the corporation. The former has been responsible for some of the most well-regarded entries in the Assassin's Creed series along with key entries in the Far Cry franchise.

The latter, meanwhile, worked on the excellent Assassin's Creed Shadows and also developed the underrated Switch gem Immortals Fenyx Rising.

GamesIndustry.biz states that the layoffs account for less than 4% of the total workforce at the studios, and that the employees affected were working on projects that had either been cancelled or significantly changed.

Here's the statement provided by Ubisoft:.

Sources indicate that "Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations. As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

It has been revealed that "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

Ubisoft's next major release is Rayman Legends Retold, a reimagined remake of the 2013 classic Rayman Legends, developed in collaboration by Ubisoft Milan and Montpellier.

#63580. Latest Update: Toy Story 3 Remaster Highlights How Movie Games Should Be Done

Latest Update: Toy Story 3 Remaster Highlights How Movie Games Should Be Done

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toy Story 3 is often regarded as one of the better games based on a movie.
  • It has been revealed that not only bring those games back, but bundle them together.
  • Industry observers note that for decades, movie tie-in games were commonplace.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toy Story 3 is often regarded as one of the better games based on a movie. A legitimately great 3D platformer that also immerses fans of the films in its world in ways that not many other tie-in games have ever managed to pull off. That’s why those of us who played it when it originally released were thrilled to find out it was part of Digital Eclipse’s surprising effort to bring pretty much all past Toy Story games to modern platforms.

It has been revealed that not only bring those games back, but bundle them together. The Retro Roundup, which combines all of the older games from the ‘90s and early ‘00s into one collection, and a remaster of Toy Story 3 for modern platforms. Best of all, the Roundup and the remaster can be bought as part of the same bundle, not just digitally, but physically, too.

Industry observers note that for decades, movie tie-in games were commonplace. Almost expected, particularly for the bigger Disney blockbusters. Aladdin, Hercules, Tarzan - they all had games that were released alongside their movies, giving fans another way to experience what they had just seen on the big screen.

That tradition has all but died out for several reasons. Trying to release a game and a movie at the same time is no longer possible, largely due to how long it takes to make games that would be considered worthy of substantial-budget blockbusters. Even if a developer were to hit the ground running the second the mere idea for a movie was uttered, that movie would still end up getting made long before the game was even close to being finished, likely by a margin of years.

Industry observers note that it’s why Toy Story 3 was probably one of the last true movie tie-in games we will ever get, which is somewhat ironic as it’s also one of the best. The trouble is, especially now with the release of its remaster, people are looking back on it and longing for another era where movies can have tie-in games released alongside them. It’s not the feeling of long-lost nostalgia we should be focusing on when playing this remaster, though. Developers and movie studios should be looking at what Disney and Avalanche did with that original game, what Digital Eclipse has done with the remaster, and using all of that as the blueprint for the future of movie games.

Even though the Toy Story 3 game and movie were released at the same time, the former isn’t just a game version of the latter. It’s effectively a love letter to the entire series, or at least the original trilogy, that pulls from those first three beloved movies. Its developers were given more freedom, which is how we wound up with the more open Woody’s Roundup area, one of the - if not the - main reasons the game was so popular.

The game didn’t need to release alongside the movie to be a success, something its Complete Edition has now proved 16 years later. Those who played the original have been reminded of just how good it was, and how it told a separate Toy Story story while remaining faithful to the films, and Disney now has a shiny new polished version to point new, younger fans towards not just when a new Toy Story movie is released, but whenever they need to.

Sources indicate that that’s the lesson that other studios which have all-but given up on movie games really need to try and learn from. That you don’t need to pull off the almost-impossible and try to get the launch of a movie and its game to perfectly align. What’s more notable is making sure that game is good and can stand the test of time. If so, you can not only release it whenever, but whenever you need it again, you have something to point to. Or, if it’s been long enough, you can give it the remaster treatment like Toy Story 3.

Sources indicate that I wouldn’t even be averse to seeing Toy Story 3 dusted off and remastered a second time a decade from now, perhaps to give Toy Story fans who haven’t even been born yet something to play two console generations from now when the sixth, seventh, and eighth movies are released. Add an extra area to Woody’s Roundup. Throw in a few more story missions. It’s certainly a lot easier than making a whole new game from scratch, which is the problem that has effectively ended the movie video game era.

Recent findings suggest that I appreciate that “Hey, just make a game that’s as good as Toy Story 3 and you’ll be set for life” is easier said than done. The thing is, I don’t think anyone is even trying. Just look at the excitement surrounding the reveal of the Coco world in Kingdom Hearts 4. There’s a Coco sequel coming, and a game like Toy Story 3 set in that world could be huge, even if it doesn’t line up with the release of its sequel. Sadly, I think Coco’s inclusion in KH is the closest we’ll ever get to a video game set in Disney’s Land of the Dead.

6 JRPGs That Got Snubbed at The Game Awards 2026

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1257 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As has already been publicly revealed, DualShockers is part of The Game Awards jury, so while I have some say in which games get nominated, I am just one voice among hundreds of journalists and many, many outlets.
  • With that in mind, I put together a list of JRPGs that got snubbed at The Game Awards 2026.
  • Sources indicate that it was a massive joy to see Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter earn a nomination for Best Role Playing Game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As has already been publicly revealed, DualShockers is part of The Game Awards jury, so while I have some say in which games get nominated, I am just one voice among hundreds of journalists and many, many outlets. And just because I sit on the jury doesn't mean I agree with every outcome. Speaking from personal experience, none of the games I nominated for Game of the Year made the cut, and fair enough, my ballot was mostly JRPGs.

With that in mind, I put together a list of JRPGs that got snubbed at The Game Awards 2026. You will find titles overlooked entirely, with no nominations, alongside JRPGs that earned a spot in one category but deserved recognition in others. That isn't to say the nominees didn't earn their accolades, but as usual, JRPGs keep getting neglected at these events in favor of mainstream juggernauts that sometimes fall short of the sheer excellence found in B-side JRPGs.

Sources indicate that it was a massive joy to see Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter earn a nomination for Best Role Playing Game. I recognize that landing a Game of the Year nod would have been a tall order, and that is completely okay. However, if there is one thing the entire Trails series excels at, it is total dedication to its story, character development, and overarching narrative. With that in mind, leaving it out of Best Narrative feels borderline criminal.

Industry observers note that the entire heart of Trails beats through its storytelling. 2nd Chapter picks up right where Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter left off, expanding across Liberl and the growing threats of Ouroboros while diving intimately into each party member's backstory. It's gripping and enthralling, and even though it can occasionally be a slow burn and a bit bloated, the narrative payoff is sensational. Across all the Trails games I have played (seven so far), the series has never once missed the mark on its climaxes and final chapters, a feat worthy of serious praise.

Industry observers note that one of the strangest choices at this year's TGAs was seeing Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave land in Best Role Playing Game, especially considering Fire Emblem Engage previously competed in Best Sim/Strategy. I heard compelling arguments from a friend suggesting that because the RPG elements in Fortune's Weave were pushed further into the spotlight, the jury may have deemed it a better fit for the RPG category. Still, I suspect it was simply an oversight.

It has been revealed that to me, it would have made far more sense for Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave to compete in Best Sim/Strategy, since being a tactical strategy RPG is the franchise's entire identity. There are two major reasons for this: first, if it hadn't taken a slot in Best RPG, another deserving JRPG could have slipped in, such as the very next entry on this list. Second, looking at the current Best Sim/Strategy lineup might leave you scratching your head, since the nominees barely seem connected to one another. What do Pokémon Pokopia, Mewgenics, and Star Wars Zero Firm actually have in common? Nothing, aside from sharing a TGA category.

Sources indicate that following my train of thought about Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave ideally competing in Best Sim/Strategy instead of Best RPG, I could easily picture The Adventures of Elliot: The Millennium Tales sliding into that open RPG slot. I realize the title, The Adventures, might make it sound like a pure action-adventure game. Yet, Square Enix officially classifies it as an RPG, and gaming outlets generally follow suit.

Sources indicate that square Enix crafted an action RPG utilizing the HD-2D visual style, and the result turned out wonderfully. While its review averages hovered around 78, which explains why it missed out on nominations, I firmly believe the game deserved far more love. It is colorful and whimsical, brimming with a nostalgic sense of adventure and an intriguing narrative spanning multiple timelines (even if it completely glosses over the classic paradoxes of time travel). Then again, maybe this is just me wanting to shine a brighter spotlight on HD-2D projects so Square Enix keeps investing in smaller original IPs.

Look, I will be the first to admit that Brigandine Abyss is simply an okay game. It is solid, and I had plenty of fun clearing two campaigns, though I didn't get nearly as much mileage out of its replayability as I did with Brigandine: The Legend of Runersia. Still, since I already started ranting about the strategy genre above, I might as well throw more fuel onto a fire of my own making. Do we need a dedicated Strategy/Tactical category separated from Simulation games? Runersia. Still, since I already started ranting about the strategy genre above, I might as well add more fuel to the fire of my own making. Do we need a dedicated Strategy/Tactical category separated from Simulation games? Hard to say, though several tactical JRPGs could definitely benefit from the spotlight.

Sources indicate that brigandine Abyss is nothing short of a miracle, truly. The original Brigandine debuted on the PS1 and remained completely obscure, even among hardcore enthusiasts. Against all odds, Happinet revived the dormant IP with The Legend of Runersia, which apparently performed well enough to greenlight another mainline follow-up: Brigandine Abyss. If The Game Awards ever introduces a category like Second Wind or Back From the Dead, Brigandine would easily earn a spot on the ballot.

It has been revealed that I know seeing two Trails games nominated in the same year would sound wild, especially since the franchise only recently began gaining wider global recognition thanks to its remakes, but Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter could run only because the modern mainline entries came first. Do you enjoy the seamless blend of real-time field action and command-based turn combat? That hybrid system was born in Trails through Daybreak and carried forward into every subsequent release.

In a recent development, trails beyond the Horizon continues the overarching saga that began in Trails in the Sky, which makes it a baffling place to jump in if you haven't been following the story. That would be like starting The Lord of the Rings with The Return of the King. Nihon Falcom makes minimal effort to recap past events, yet largely assumes enthusiasts have played the earlier chapters (which is precisely why they are working so hard to remake older entries). Hopefully, in the coming years, we will see non-remake Trails entries breaking into major RPG categories as well.

Industry observers note that honestly, it is well past time The Game Awards introduced a dedicated Best Remake/Remaster category, as in my experience, these projects are often judged unfairly by the jury when stacked directly against brand-newly introduced releases. Without diving too deep into that debate, if Dragon Quest VII Reimagined had been a brand-new original title rather than a remake, I am almost certain it would have landed a TGA nomination, particularly in Best RPG.

It has been revealed that dragon Quest VII Reimagined was, well, thoughtfully reimagined for modern audiences. The original release was notoriously bloated, taking hours just to reach your very first combat encounter. While the remake trimmed away a few islands from the classic version, those cuts worked wonders for the pacing. Both combat and character progression were cleanly streamlined, and random encounters were ditched in favor of visible monsters roaming the map. Dragon Quest VII Reimagined is a phenomenal achievement that delights newcomers and longtime veterans alike.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that nongshim RedForce have brought 2022 world champion Deft back to the LCK and paired him again with Kingen and Pyosik.
  • Sources indicate that kim ‘Deft’ Hyuk-kyu’s signing was confirmed on 19 November.
  • Sources indicate that the deal reunites him with two members of the DRX side that won the 2022 World Championship.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that nongshim RedForce have brought 2022 world champion Deft back to the LCK and paired him again with Kingen and Pyosik. The move follows an eighth-place 2026 for the club and comes days after BLG ended Korea's four-year hold on the World Championship.

Sources indicate that kim ‘Deft’ Hyuk-kyu’s signing was confirmed on 19 November. The club used its official social media channels to make the announcement. Deft began his military service after the 2024 season ended.

Sources indicate that the deal reunites him with two members of the DRX side that won the 2022 World Championship. Jungler Hong ‘Pyosik’ Chang-hyeon joined later the same day, alongside support Moon ‘Andil’ Gwan-bin. Top laner Hwang ‘Kingen’ Seong-hoon had re-signed a day earlier.

In a recent development, deft’s signing was unveiled at 7pm. The Pyosik and Andil additions that followed completed Nongshim’s five-man starting line-up, Inven Global reported. Mid laner Seon ‘Calix’ Hyeon-bin provides continuity. He has been with the organisation since 2021 and extended his deal on 18 November.

Sources indicate that deft brings a long winning record. He made his debut with MVP Blue in 2013. His titles include the LCK, the LPL, the Mid-Season Invitational and the 2022 World Championship.

It has been revealed that kingen first joined Nongshim for the 2025 season. Pyosik arrives after a difficult 2026 at DN SOOPers. That team lost a run of matches, and rookie Sharvel took his starting place.

The move had been signalled. About a month before the announcement, Sheep Esports reported from Korean sources that Nongshim planned to sign Deft. The same report stated rookie AD carry Diable would need a latest team.

The signings mark a sharp change of direction after a poor year. Once the league campaign was over, the team lasted just a single match in the play-ins.

Sources indicate that the deal lands days after a setback for the whole league. Bilibili Gaming’s victory over Gen.G came at the Barclays Center in Latest York. It gave the organisation its first Summoner’s Cup.

BLG won all four of its series against LCK teams at the tournament. Every LCK seed fell to the Chinese side on its way to the trophy. The title is also the LPL’s first since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

'Deft' has signed a contract as the new ADC of NS RedForce LCK Team.

Please look forward to and support Deft, who has written latest history with an unbreakable spirit through countless trials, as he takes on new challenges and delivers great… pic.twitter.com/bHa1uJWwKV.

— NS RedForce (@NS_RedForce) November 19, 2026.

For Nongshim, a line-up built around three 2022 champions now has an international calendar to aim at. Riot Games has moved First Stand 2027 from Southeast Asia to China and renamed it First Stand: All In. It will be a one-off expanded edition with more teams and players.

Spain gets its debut as a Mid-Season Invitational host in 2027, with Valencia’s Feria de Valencia as the venue. Before that, Riot prepares to publish First Stand: All In’s format and qualification process in January.

    #63571. Tech Report: 10 Hard to Beat Sega Genesis JRPGs

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1653 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: 10 Hard to Beat Sega Genesis JRPGs

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1653 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that while many of us played our first JRPGs on PS1 or PS2, they existed way before then.
    • There's a good mix even with these JRPG adventures, which feature sword and sorcery fantasy, far flung future and others besides.
    • In a recent development, as for how they're ranked, we dug deep to find critical reception, and did our best to sort these JRPGs accordingly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that while many of us played our first JRPGs on PS1 or PS2, they existed way before then. The catch was, many of the JRPGs on older systems were incredibly experimental games. They were less clearly defined, but still worthwhile. That especially applies for the Sega Genesis, which featured many hard to beat JRPGs.

    There's a good mix even with these JRPG adventures, which feature sword and sorcery fantasy, far flung future and others besides. No matter what, though, they all featured some capacity to upgrade your characters, and many were turn-based as well.

    In a recent development, as for how they're ranked, we dug deep to find critical reception, and did our best to sort these JRPGs accordingly. So join me in my time machine as we head back to the glory days of the Sega Genesis with these hard to beat JRPGs!

    While the Dungeons & Dragons series has come a long way, it's fascinating to see where it started, at least in videogames. And though Dungeons & Dragons: Warriors of the Eternal Sun was mechanically a pretty weird JRPG, it featured a pretty engaging plot.

    It starts with typical warfare against lowly goblins, then has the human army warped to a mysterious land of the Eternal Sun. Meanwhile, something called the Burrower is driving all your allies insane. It's surprisingly Lovecraftian, and quite neat, especially from back in the Sega Genesis era.

    This JRPG has a lot of understandable dungeon crawler energy, with players mustering a party of four different characters whose race and class determines everything. And like any good JRPG, as you level up, you'll learn powerful newly introduced skills, though much is decided by the RNG roll of a dice.

    It has been revealed that even though I'm not a huge fan of the whole Mystery Dungeon craze, I can see the general appeal. I discovered them with the Pokemon offshoots, but they started way sooner. One of the first examples is simply called Fatal Labyrinth.

    It has been revealed that it's about chasing a vicious dragon that guards a Holy Goblet, and safely navigating 30 floors of dangers to get there. Enemies don't move or act until you do, so there's inherent strategy in Fatal Labyrinth. More unique, you'll do well to discover whether scrolls and potions hurt or harm you, and using them accordingly.

    Perhaps the most charmingly old school aspect of the game is that gold only serves one purpose – blinging out your funeral when you die! So make sure to stock up on vital food and powerful gear, and maybe your journey won't have an ignominious end.

    Sources indicate that in a way, The Immortal makes a better novel than a videogame. It's the tale of a call from deep within a labyrinth from the wizard Mordamir. You're not the person he called, named Dunric, but you'll do! Along the way, you'll navigate through several levels, ride magic carpets, and discover the true nightmare of what happened.

    According to recent reports, like any good JRPG, there's NPCs here, and you can even cast magic spells to roast your enemies. Those include the likes of goblins, flesh-eating slimes, shades and even a diabolical dragon. Also surprising for the era, The Immortal was surprisingly graphic and violent at times.

    According to recent reports, while the game features lots of fun fantasy elements, it's also painfully linear, which made some feel it didn't do enough for the genre. Still, a good early attempt, and one that experimented in some meaningful ways.

    I think it's fair to say that The Lord of the Rings inspired Sword of Vermilion on the Sega Genesis. The game features King Tsarkon, who is warped by a magical ring, and twisted to evil ends. A valiant knight named Blade saves the good king's child, and then 18 years later, counsels the prince on his deathbed. It's up to him to honor his dead father and his valiant protector.

    Recent findings suggest that as for how Sword of Vermilion actually plays, it has a lot of ARPG mechanics. Furthermore, the gameplay shifts depending on a variety of circumstances, and alternates between top down and side views for the exploration and boss battles.

    While the game has a lot of fun arcade energy, the graphics weren't seen as a high point, even back when it first released. On the plus side, it was also a console exclusive, meaning only those who owned a Sega Genesis experienced this classic JRPG.

    I'm usually a fan of when developers try something upcoming. But with Phantasy Star III: Generations of Doom, it was actually a brand new team brought in who hadn't worked on the previous two games. On the plus side, they tried new features like branching narrative paths and multiple endings. On the negative, in some ways this didn't feel like a Phantasy Star adventure.

    Phantasy Star III: Generations of Doom actually spans multiple generations, meaning you'll play as the descendants of your starting main character, which honestly feels a bit like Fire Emblem. Depending on who you marry, you'll continue the game with different abilities as various children.

    In a recent development, this adventure downplays the Technique system, but it makes up for it with auto-battle and an icon-based menu. Either way, this is traditional turn-based fare that, at least for me, makes me feel right at home in any JRPG adventure.

    Sources indicate that unlike the last game, Ys III: Wanderers From Ys is very much a direct follow up to the previous Ys adventures. It features Adol Christin, mysterious statues and the advent of a brutal demon named Galbalan. The game also handles stats, equipment and experience the same as the other games.

    Where Ys III: Wanderers From Ys stands apart is that it utilizes a side-scrolling view instead of the more traditional top-down style. Also, you can't just auto attack anymore, and instead need to pres a button to have Adol swing his blade or cast spells.

    While the game can be a bit grindy and repetitive, those who were already fans of the Ys series were very happy with this adventure. It could have done more to branch out, perhaps, but sometimes if it's not broken, you don't need to fix anything.

    Sources indicate that whenever you hear that Treasure developed a game, you have to pay attention. They make some of the most creative games out there, though usually it's more platformers than JRPGs. In fairness, Light Crusader is a bit of an odd duck, combining the JRPG genre with isometric graphics and action adventure mechanics.

    You play Sir David, who is trying to save the kidnapped citizens of Green Row. He can run and jump, swing his blade and generally beat up monsters. But he's also capable of casting elemental magic. They can be cast individually or combined, buffing David or healing him, amongst other uses.

    Along the way, you'll discover the entire game is about the slighted advances of a diabolical wizard. He wanted desperately to marry the Queen of Green Row, and in his petulance, eventually summons a demon. Definitely a quirky adventure, but a memorable one, even years and years later.

    Sources indicate that it took me a long while to get to Langrisser, a tactical series as popular in some spheres as Fire Emblem or Tactics Ogre. It didn't start with that name, though. Originally, it was called Warsong, and it was a pretty substantial deal on the Sega Genesis. It's a fun but pretty brutal tactical JRPG adventure.

    According to recent reports, like many brutal games, Warsong features permadeath, meaning if you're not careful, you could lose some of your best characters forever. Your commanders determine what units you can bring into battle, such as powerful Griffons.

    Ultimately, careful strategy rewards you with powerful upgrades to your commanders, including changing their classes. If all that wasn't enough, Warsong also features great music composed by Noriyuki Iwadare. A great game if you're strong enough to get through it relatively unscathed.

    There aren't all that many times I get really jealous about console exclusivity these days. But one of those classics I wish I had played back in the day was Shining Force II. It wasn't just good, but it was considered one of the best tactical JRPGs of all time.

    Some of the reasons people felt that way was due to how open-ended the game was, as well as the great visual flair. It alternated between top-down while exploring, and side scrolling during combat. Either way, the game was challenging, and forced you to lead Bowie and friends carefully.

    According to recent reports, as for the plot, Shining Force II takes place 55 years after Shining Force Gaiden: Final Conflict, and is about Zeon's mayhem. But even if you didn't play the previous games, this is one tactical adventure that holds up, though it's also far from an easy time.

    According to recent reports, one of the more iconic games I played back in the day was Alundra. It was sort of like Zelda, but not really, and it really captivated me. One game that came before it was called Landstalker, a game about a treasure hunter named Nigel.

    It has been revealed that while Landstalker may not seem like a JRPG at first, there are a couple of reasons it qualifies as one. Even though you don't level up by traditional means, you can take on sidequests to improve your stats. There's also ways to improve your health, and even equip more powerful gear. A lot of it just requires a desire to explore as much as possible.

    Much of the game's overall challenge comes from devious death traps and gnarly puzzles, not to mention challenging boss battles. Definitely a strange old-school JRPG, but one that managed to delight fans by taking plenty of creative risks.

    The MOBA genre is competitive in every sense and Quantic Dream is trying to break into it with a Magic the Gathering-esque spin on the format. Players build a deck of cards before queuing into teams of 3, then face off as battling mages, summoning creatures, building fortifications and casting spells rather than choosing a Hero with unique abilities in the traditional MOBA style.

    Beta content includes a latest map, 6 new spells and 5 new summon creatures for your deck, as well as 3 new buildings too.

    Also newly introduced for this second closed beta is an introduction and tutorial for some of the game’s finer details, as well as a text chat for strategising and much-needed player reporting system to go with it.     Latest Update: Rob Run Is Surging On Steam As PC Players Look For A GTA 6 Alternative

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that rockstar still hasn't confirmed when GTA 6 will launch on PC, and judging by past releases, it could take anywhere from 7 to 19 months.
    • In a recent development, rob Run, a cops-and-robbers "crime sandbox" where every single cop and robber is played by a "living breathing human," released on Steam earlier this month.
    • On November 15, Rob Run hit a peak of over half-a-million players with a 549,661 CCU, and has continued to hold firm while PC players watch from the sidelines as every single social media feed is flooded with posts about GTA 6.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that rockstar still hasn't confirmed when GTA 6 will launch on PC, and judging by past releases, it could take anywhere from 7 to 19 months. However, one game is already filling the void.

    In a recent development, rob Run, a cops-and-robbers "crime sandbox" where every single cop and robber is played by a "living breathing human," released on Steam earlier this month. It was a pretty successful release for Last Day on Earth and Frostborn developer Kefir, with a 23,000 peak on November 4 rising to 43,000 within just a few days — a number that only skyrocketed as GTA 6 got closer and closer.

    On November 15, Rob Run hit a peak of over half-a-million players with a 549,661 CCU, and has continued to hold firm while PC players watch from the sidelines as every single social media feed is flooded with posts about GTA 6.

    To put those numbers into perspective, it's the fourth most-played game on the platform right now, competing with heavy-hitters like CS2 and Apex Legends:.

    Sources indicate that admittedly, Rob Run is closer to something like GTA Online (specifically, RP) than GTA 6, but it has all the hallmarks: bank robberies, police chases, convenience store stick-ups, and the rags-to-riches criminal enterprise story that defines so many Grand Theft Auto games. "In just one week, you can go from being a regular thug to the boss of the server's largest organization," the description reads. "And then start over — with fresh experience, allies, and a more ambitious plan to seize power.".

    Recent findings suggest that it sounds like a solid alternative to GTA 6 on paper, even if it doesn't quite measure up to the charm of NotGTAV, the Snake-like parody where you drive around in a Tesco car park that kept us going while we waited for Los Santos, but there's a big asterisk here. Developer Kefir admits to using AI "in the creation of certain graphic elements," and the 'Mixed' reviews paint a stark picture of cheaters running rampant and a completely unwelcoming community that have made the game impenetrable for newcomers.

    "Half enjoyable AI slop rendered completely unplayable due to the worst cheating crisis I've seen since Counter-Strike," reads one review.

    It has been revealed that "Great concept, ruined by the community," notes another. "Cops just kill on sight (KOS) the moment they see you wearing a mask. Criminals aren't any better. Both sides constantly camp selling areas and extraction points, making it almost pointless to even try playing the game as intended.".

    "Every store you try to rob is already robbed or you get shot by another player just getting out of your car," warns one reviewer. "Tried to live an honest life and play as a cop but everyone is already playing as a cop so it will not let you. As a latest player, all I could do is drive around and return to Lenny's cause any time I slowed down I got rammed by some other robber.".

    In a recent development, plenty of reviews raise eyebrows that AI appears to have been used more than the disclosure lets on, while complaining of connection issues and long maintenance windows interrupting the experience. Kefir is already working to address some of these problems, adding a more overt report button, improving servers, and limiting voice chat to target toxicity, while also adding more methods to detect cheaters, but the negative reviews only continue to pour in.

    "I've never experienced this many hackers in a game before," a review from earlier today claimed. "Within 30 minutes of a server going live, people are already using aimbot and pulling bank heists. Servers not being region locked makes things even worse. The game is also practically unplayable for solo players. Winning a 1v2 is possible, but a 1v3 is impossible [...] The game is fun and has potential, but between hackers, camping, and the huge advantage groups have over solo players, it's honestly more frustrating than enjoyable. Not worth the headache in its current state.".

    So, while it might be a solid free-to-play alternative to GTA 6 right now, the reality of Rob Run is a game plagued by overt AI use, cheaters, and a KOS problem that makes DayZ look tame.

    Industry observers note that cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

    Cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” says game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

    In a recent development, in addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

    Mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another significant content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

    If you couldn’t guess already, the fresh theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

    The massive upcoming story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

    In a recent development, these are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

    The Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

    It has been revealed that the other significant addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

    In a recent development, chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

    You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a newly introduced Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

    As with every major revision, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

    If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love.
    • As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year.
    • It has been revealed that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

    As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

    It has been revealed that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the organization's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be declared tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

    According to recent reports, this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

    According to recent reports, last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

    According to recent reports, what do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

    8 Most Unhinged NPC Inner Truths From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
