    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, you’ve spent time wandering around Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and you decided to pay the Happy Mask Salesman a visit.
    • Industry observers note that what does this mask do?
    • Listening to the inner truths of the game’s various NPCs can get a bit wild, but these are the most unhinged and strange thoughts to be found in Hyrule.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, you’ve spent time wandering around Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and you decided to pay the Happy Mask Salesman a visit. He gave you a few masks, you made a few sales, and you have received the Mask of Truth in return.

    Industry observers note that what does this mask do? Well, it reveals the inner thoughts of the game’s various NPCs. I am not sure if you have paid attention to Nintendo games recently, but they have been adding in some interesting NPC dialogue.

    Listening to the inner truths of the game’s various NPCs can get a bit wild, but these are the most unhinged and strange thoughts to be found in Hyrule.

    According to recent reports, if you walk around the town square in Castle Town, you can find some rather colorful NPCs, but one of the most unassuming of them is the old woman who stares at the fountain. She seems so sweet, but she is actually a thief.

    Listening to her inner thoughts, you see that they say, “The quality of the items people are losing has really gone downhill recently… Is that a recession indicator?”.

    This hits a little close to home considering many have questioned if the U.S. is entering a recession. Along with this, it is obvious that she is taking some of the goods that people have lost and keeping them for herself.

    If you continue your search around the fountain in Castle Town, you can find a young couple who are dancing. While they seem rather sweet, their inner thoughts tell a completely different story.

    According to recent reports, when you read the thoughts of the woman, it will say that she hopes that the man doesn’t break her heart. It is a sad thought to be had because she is clearly worried about her future.

    When you read the man’s thoughts, you see they say, “Wait… What was this one’s name again?” Clearly, this isn’t his only crush, and he is stringing this poor woman along so he has someone to dance with. Yes… dance with.

    Recent findings suggest that some of the guards around Castle Town aren’t very excited about their job. In fact, some of them find it boring doing patrols all the time. One guard in particular thinks about it pretty frequently.

    Industry observers note that when interacting with the guard in the room with the pots, his inner truth will say, “Guards… Soldiers… Heroes… It’s their fault there’s so much peace around here. Hm… What if I…”.

    The thought trails off after that, but you can clearly tell what he is thinking about. The man wants some chaos, and he is clearing thinking about being the cause of said chaos if something doesn’t happen soon.

    You may have seen the bearded man wandering around Castle Town in the past and Kakariko Village in the future. His beard is magnificent, and he will definitely tell you about it. However, he is secretly questioning its cleanliness.

    When you listen to his inner thoughts, they say, “I wonder if it’s true that beards are about as dirty as toilets…” For someone with such a massive beard, he shouldn’t be thinking that he is dirty, unless he wants to shave it off.

    This is a massive contrast to what he will tell you when you speak to him, as he will typically say that he has a fantastic beard, and will even offer to locate Ganondorf.

    According to recent reports, shiro is one of the many NPCs you can find around Kakariko Village, and you also help him out by rescuing him from the Gerudo as an adult. Well, he isn’t the happiest carpenter around. In fact, he is rather depressed.

    His inner thoughts read, “How does one escape their own dreary life? ‘Cause I can’t do this forever.” Granted, he didn’t seem the happiest when I rescued him from the Gerudo, but I never would have guessed that he was this depressed.

    Looking into his thoughts, he seems like he could use some therapy because it sounds like he has been hanging around Lumiose City in Pokémon Legends: Z-A for too long.

    Industry observers note that there’s a pair of laughing men who appear in Castle Town and Kakariko. No matter what is happening, the pair consistently laugh at one another. They typically talk about stories they find funny, with the one laughing at the other for getting caught sneaking into the castle or falling off a horse.

    However, when you read their inner thoughts, the one says, “It’s exhausting wearing this forced smile all the time.” The other one will remark about how he knows his friend’s smile is fake.

    It’s sad that they continue to laugh constantly. Maybe they should just try to chill out for once and give up on the laughter. Are they cursed? Maybe they are cursed.

    According to recent reports, if you have explored Kakariko Village, you are for sure aware of the cucco lady. All of her cuccos get out of the pen, and you must go rescue them for a reward. In the future, she is living with a questionable character.

    If you use the Mask of Truth while you are an adult, you will catch her inner thoughts. They say, “That guy who lives with me always makes the most intense eye contact. He must really love cuccos…”.

    Industry observers note that what she is describing does not sound healthy at all. In fact, it sounds almost like something bad is going to happen and she is just waiting for the inevitable. Maybe she should choose a different place to live or kick the guy out.

    Sources indicate that there is an old man who likes to wander around Castle Town. He will go in and out of shops, but mostly he will walk around the fountain. Just be careful listening to his thoughts because he has a particular woman on his mind.

    His inner thoughts read, “This kid… The mask’s neat and all, but I’m more interested in finding a particular damsel…” While it doesn’t seem so bad at first, if you talk to him, you can piece things together.

    Recent findings suggest that talking to him, he will make remarks about how he is looking for a lady who can make a potion, and will gawk at how beautiful she is. He will also casually talk about how we are at the age to be thinking about that.

    Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming enhancement, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in New Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

    Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

    The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for Newly introduced Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

    The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

    Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two latest Agents being introduced in this patch belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

    Industry observers note that sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

    Aria is the other latest arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

    Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

    Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

    Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a upcoming game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

    According to recent reports, beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a upcoming outfit for Pan Yinhu.

    Recent findings suggest that the substantial event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

    Recent findings suggest that though it may seem like we just had a significant life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

    According to recent reports, the game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

    Seed Sparkle Lab confirmed today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

    It has been revealed that the developer stated to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

    The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

    Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

    Recent findings suggest that speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

    On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

    Seed Sparkle Lab indicates you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

    According to recent reports, you can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

    • Sources indicate that it sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off.
    • On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.
    • At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that it sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

    On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

    At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

    As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

    It has been revealed that this already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

    Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is at the moment number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

    It has been revealed that there are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

    Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

    Industry observers note that critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

    Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Infinity Nikki is making headlines with its latest controversy about including Maye Musk in their 3.0 introductory trailer for Chinese players, but it seems that there are actually great surprises, according to other livestreams.

    Today, in the main dev livestream for Chinese players (translated by YouTuber Whimsy Haven in English), which is where most things are revealed before the patch actually drops.

    In the Infinity Nikki universe, people are coming up with theories and release schedules, where we are all travelling to next, and what the next abilities are.

    With Grand Theft Auto 6 grabbing everyone’s attention, it seems like a genius nod that the cosy styling game decided to show its claws and add guns to the mix.

    Nikki, in all her infinite universes and extended lore, is no stranger to guns, but so far it has been discussed heavily by fans whether Infold would take a safer approach and not give Nikki guns in the latest game.

    Recent findings suggest that thankfully for all lovers of shooters, that is not the case. Nikki already has a huge backdrop of dark lore, and it only makes sense that they would dim the vibes in-game even further with the addition of guns to use against foes and Esselings.

    The addition of a pink Barbie-esque convertible makes the Grand Theft Auto comparisons even funnier for fans of both, as we are all consumed by the hype for the Rockstar instant classic.

    Recent findings suggest that unlike Rockstar, Infinity Nikki fans also got a glimpse of her dancing with a latest character, which looked very suspiciously like Oscar from Rose of Versailles. Some fans are taking it as a further nod to the queer fans and those locked into Nikki lore, where rumours of her sexuality have floated from the early games.

    Industry observers note that but of course, the main star of the show is Nikki and the latest character using guns. Now, with her new 'gal pal,' you can switch guns on the go as you fight foes, from a semi-automatic pistol to a short-barreled shotgun, as shown in the livestream.

    This is not the first gun in Infinity Nikki, as in 2.4 Nikki had a hunting shotgun which would only show up when the ability was used and wasn’t as flexible, leaving many fans disappointed but hopeful for more guns further on.

    Infinity Nikki fans also got a glimpse of dancing with a new character, which looked very suspiciously like Oscar from Rose of Versailles.

    The other upcoming weapons seem to be wizard staffs, as we have already had a few wands in accessories rather than actual weapons, which makes sense in a game with a heavy dress-up mechanic.

    The controversy with Maye Musk, Elon Musk’s mother, certainly put a dent in Infinity Nikki’s reputation, and the conversation between fans and devs has been strained. Nikki and her games are no strangers to controversy, and with the latest fiasco with Love and Deep Space still ongoing about Valko, only time will tell how Infold will react to all the communication between them and fans.

    Infold has generally been receptive to Infinity Nikki fans, who have been asking for guns, darker storylines, more romance (even if only hinted at), among other things.

    Sadly, we’re not sure if you can do drive-by shooting Grand Theft Auto style yet, as the footage of the car mostly focused on the streets of Cicia, but knowing Nikki and how you can summon the unicorn, bike, or motorcycle in different areas, the car should be able to breeze through weird forest terrain.

    It may make sense to ask for drive-by shooting mechanics in the next questionnaires for more fun updates, as the devs do listen to what the fans want to see next.

    It has been revealed that all in all, interesting things are happening in the next massive Infinity Nikki upgrade! No mention of poor Giovanni, though; he’s still in the basement.

    Infinity Nikki is available on PC, macOS, PlayStation 5, and iOS and Android phones.

    The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

    Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

    The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

    It has been revealed that the imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

    The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

    Industry observers note that much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

    As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

    According to recent reports, version 4.0 introduces two latest 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

    General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

    Industry observers note that her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

    According to recent reports, the other fresh arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

    When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

    It has been revealed that she also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

    Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

    Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the upcoming outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

    In a recent development, if you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

    Recent findings suggest that shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports. The non-partner organisation is now one win from the playoffs that decide a guaranteed São Paulo Kickoff place.

    The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

    The result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that noted it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

    Sources indicate that the Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

    Industry observers note that shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

    Across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

    The organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

    According to recent reports, the prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

    Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

    Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

    The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

    Industry observers note that the first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

    Sources indicate that the ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

    According to recent reports, the more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

    Sources indicate that badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

    In a recent development, heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

    We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

    #63544. Tech Report: 10 Best Metroidvania Boss Fights of the 2020s (So Far)

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1625 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: 10 Best Metroidvania Boss Fights of the 2020s (So Far)

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Modern Metroidvanias, largely influenced by Soulsborne titles' formula, have heavily emphasized boss fights as the core of their gameplay, and I'm quite happy about it.
    • I can't deny my absolute fascination with formidable adversaries that test my reflexes, adaptability, and resolve, and this genre in particular has understood those keys better than most.
    • With each passing year, we not only receive more outstanding Metroidvanias but also specifically more experiences that utilize this gameplay concept to its fullest potential, usually representing the high points of their respective adventures.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Modern Metroidvanias, largely influenced by Soulsborne titles' formula, have heavily emphasized boss fights as the core of their gameplay, and I'm quite happy about it.

    I can't deny my absolute fascination with formidable adversaries that test my reflexes, adaptability, and resolve, and this genre in particular has understood those keys better than most.

    With each passing year, we not only receive more outstanding Metroidvanias but also specifically more experiences that utilize this gameplay concept to its fullest potential, usually representing the high points of their respective adventures.

    Therefore, if you're like me and fascinated by a good duel with health bars and numerous phases, I invite you to read this list of the ten best Metroidvania boss fights of the 2020s (so far).

    Well Dweller is a magnificent video game that, as the pinnacle of Kyle Thompson's craft, is brimming with spectacular yet accessible special bosses, such as The Queen.

    The plethora of sequences, attacks, and projectiles that unfold during your final encounter is breathtaking, truly connecting with the idea that royalty rules with an iron fist because they actually possess the power to dominate others.

    Disfiguring the face of your family's kidnapper is fitting for a title that's cozy on the surface but profoundly dark beneath it, materialized in a demanding fight in terms of positioning and movement that makes you feel like you're constantly swimming against the tide.

    While the bosses in Well Dweller wouldn't be my primary reason for recommending this gem, The Queen, in particular, demonstrates the wide variety that Metroidvanias can offer, rather than simply reducing everything to dodging and attacking in between.

    The entirety of Shinobi: Art of Vengeance is a moving marvel with choreography worthy of the best action sequences of recent years, thanks to the tremendous animations and magnificent display of audiovisual effects for bosses like Lord Ruse.

    Its imposing arena and visual design provide the perfect backdrop to prepare you for the epic duel this tormented villain has in store, whose tragic origin story is only surpassed by the way his darkness permeates the fight.

    What was once an honorable man surrenders his body and mind to an abject power that threatens the balance of the world, making it fitting that his fight resembles that of a ninja against a natural phenomenon capable of defying the laws of physics.

    The gameplay is very satisfying, forcing you to use all the tools and combos at your disposal to evade and attack effectively, leveraging the title's glorious combat system, where, after dominating all the combos, you can truly perform a martial aesthetic feast.

    The gimmick of having you constantly face a boss throughout a game is quite difficult to pull off successfully, but Gilroy, the Administrator from Ender Magnolia: Bloom in the Mist is a perfect example of when it's done well.

    While the game's roster of bosses is quite varied, its developers understand the magic of fighting a humanoid adversary who, true to FromSoftware's philosophy, forces you to decipher a rapid and relentless attack pattern where the slightest mistake is punished with death.

    Gilroy is a challenge that evolves in each of the three encounters, always leaving room for more secrets, until the final confrontation arrives with the full weight of the narrative, where you must fight one last battle that is as bittersweet as it is satisfying.

    Ender Magnolia is a game that relies heavily on its aesthetics, story, and music to amplify its emotional impact, so the campaign reaches its peak when you must defeat this recurring and memorable figure one last time.

    Speaking of recurring tropes throughout video game history, Tunic presents The Heir as the final boss very early in the story, allowing you to become familiar with its power while simultaneously understanding how far you are from completing your journey.

    Games with such a strong emphasis on exploration and adventure as this one must make every element contribute to the sense of progress, and nothing demonstrates your growth more than a superpowered entity with whom you gradually close the gap.

    Checking your evolution through repeated attempts over many hours is captivating, as is finally realizing you're on par and understanding the remarkable challenge it truly holds, hidden behind complex and rapid combos, diverse area attacks, and far more resistance than you initially expected.

    The Heir's fight is simple but makes the most of Tunic's functional mechanics, and the satisfaction of delivering the final blow after so many hours lost and disoriented is unparalleled.

    Ori and the Will of the Wisps constantly surpasses itself with each fresh boss, escape sequence, and scene, culminating in a Shriek encounter that ranges from breathtaking to utterly devastating.

    The franchise is a relentless litany of tragedies and victims that exact a toll on the kindness of those who suffer them, leading you to confront a majestic yet deeply traumatized owl amidst what appears to be the end of the universe.

    The screen seems to crumble as your confrontation with Shriek unfolds dynamically, with both combat and platforming sections taking place as the boss moves in and out of the frame with truly enviable dynamism.

    More than just a boss fight, the sequence feels like a genuine battle where a force of nature truly wants to defeat you; sensations enhanced by the magnificent soundtrack and the sheer madness of particles and colors displayed during the fight.

    Fighting Vahram in his godlike form inside the borders of time itself is among those images that stay with you forever, something Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown does quite regularly.

    These former brothers-in-arms clash in a magnificent duel where time freezes and reverses, beams of light and swords appear from all sides, and your adversary manipulates the laws of physics as if they were clay, making it a truly spectacular show.

    As you whittle down his health and he becomes cornered, the fight's complexity increases considerably, building to a tremendous crescendo where you feel the climax approaching and the adrenaline surging.

    Vahram is one of those bosses who can destroy you dozens of times in a row and you'll still be happy, because he's so well and precisely designed that each new opportunity to fight him again feels like a gift.

    True final bosses are usually the ultimate display of difficulty, depth, and passion that a Metroidvania has to offer, including Shii in MIO: Memories in Orbit.

    Fighting the companion who guided you throughout the story not because of some villainous adversity, but because of a genuine conflict of beliefs about what constitutes the most desirable outcome, is heartbreaking yet captivating, especially given the challenge that awaits.

    Shii lives up to his title, offering a multi-layered duel that demands you be as adept at recognizing openings as you are at dodging, jumping, dashing, grappling, flying, and more to evade its endless array of varied and omnidirectional attacks.

    The boss also flies, vanishes, glides, and crawls in an organic clash that makes the most of MIO: Memories in Orbit's environment and mechanics, resulting in an absolute delight.

    Blasphemous 2 boasts one of the most fluid and satisfying combat systems in the entire genre, but none exploit its flow state's sweet satisfaction quite like Eviterno, Last Desecrator.

    While the rest of the game is relatively manageable, this timeless warrior subverts expectations and delivers the beating of your life, proving that all the challenges you've overcome so far were just the tip of the iceberg he embodies.

    Far from the abominations and colossi you face during your crusade, the title presents, in its climax, a knight equal to you whose speed, power, and versatility demand pixel-perfect decision-making every second, regardless of your build.

    The best bosses are the ones that push you to your limits, and considering Eviterno penalizes even a millisecond off-timing or being a pixel too close, he's a clear contender for the decade's finest.

    Eigong is a mentor to our protagonist in Nine Sols both in story and gameplay, as no other encounter teaches you to appreciate its prodigious combat system so profoundly.

    There are fierce contenders throughout the campaign, though the one tasked with opposing Yi at the very end exponentially raises the demands of mechanical control, as any performance less than perfect will result in the same outcome: a return to the checkpoint.

    With three hellish phases brimming with rapid and agile movements—horizontal and vertical, parryable and unparryable, close and long range—it's an unstoppable barrage of abilities unless you know Yi's powers like the back of your hand.

    Only absolute, unwavering concentration will give you a chance against Eigong, whose defeat quickly transforms from a painful climb into one of the most magical memories a Metroidvania has ever offered.

    Being the only one on the entire list who isn't the game's final boss, which already hints at her unparalleled quality, Skarrsinger Karmelita is Hollow Knight: Silksong's highest point.

    That Team Cherry's masterpiece has the genre's best boss this decade is undeniable, with representatives like Trobbio, Second Sentinel, Cogwork Dancers, and Lace to justify it, but ultimately it's the queen of the ants who gets the recognition.

    It's a majestic encounter from the very beginning, leading you through the halls of a theater with her glorious singing, and then, after gifting you her minions as an offering to start the fight with full silk, appearing on stage to give you the concert of your life.

    The song, setting, art direction, attacks, rhythm, duration... Everything is perfectly timed to ensure a flawless experience, whether it takes you one try or a thousand (which is more likely).

    Skarrsinger Karmelita, I dare say, is among the best bosses in video game history and a perfect example of why this gameplay concept has gained so much relevance over the years.

    Nioh 3 has had a massive weekend on Steam, the type of launch you just don’t often see for Koei Tecmo games. Indeed, this has very clearly been a monumentous release for both the publisher, and developer Team Ninja.

    It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

    Industry observers note that nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. Anyone keeping up with how well the game has been received, and how much it’s been anticipated by series fans and Soulslike players, would’ve told you that it was only the beginning.

    Late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

    That’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

    In a recent development, love and Deepspace has kicked off the next significant in-game moment and is celebrating Chinese New Year with the arrival of a new 5-Star Memory Series. This year's spring-themed banner is available now until February 27, and it comes with a host of events.

    The Mortality’s Tenderness banner features five new limited-time 5-Star Memories, one each for the game’s five love interests. The theme is all about warmth, reunion, and intimacy, taking place in a Wuxia-inspired setting that's once again an alternate universe from the main story of the game.

    It has been revealed that the upcoming memory cards are Xavier: Blades with Blossoms, Zayne: Entwined Kites, Rafayel: Carved Gemheart, Sylus: Shared Lanterns, and Caleb: Clearday Return. You can pick three of the five to focus on and further pick one to guarantee on your second 5-star pull; and you can earn wish rewards by making cumulative wishes over the course of the event.

    Some of the rewards you could get include limited headwear, Limited Deepspace Wishes, and — of course — Memory-themed outfits and hairstyles inspired by the new Memories. Outside of wish rewards, the Memory Series comes with growth tasks that rewards you with in-game materials for levelling up the new cards during the event. When you reach Rank 1 for any new Memory from the banner, you’ll earn a Memory-themed outfit with a special colour that matches your chosen love interest.

    Illusio returns as part of the upcoming event, too, letting you customise the look of Kindled Moments across all five new Memories. Things you can customise include selecting the outfits and accessories for each love interest, so you can recreate Kindled Moments in your own style. As always, Kindled Moments will go back to their default look after the event ends.

    Recent findings suggest that there’s a upcoming mini-game to play, too, available only during the event. It’s called Courteous Fare, a frantic but familiar restaurant management simulation that allows you to unlock a variety of rewards.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros.
    • Recent findings suggest that skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio.

    Industry observers note that A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.

    Recent findings suggest that skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio. All this was was done, of course, to maximise the amount of IP that the corporation can access to base games on, such as Avatar: The Last Airbender, Game of Thrones, Star Trek, the DC Universe, Harry Potter, and more. Skydance Games came into existence on October 6th; it barely lasted a month as it was.

    It has been revealed that in a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company." Skydance did not disclose the number of staff affected.

    Skydance joins the ever-growing list of corporations that have mandated layoffs in the recent past, such as Microsoft, Ubisoft, and EA. Workers will bleed until there is no one left to cut. Solidarity to all affected.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Generative AI has been in the limelight for some time now, with many fearing what effect it could have on game development and employment – including Capcom veteran and Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami, apparently.

    Recent findings suggest that speaking with Inven Global in a newly introduced interview, he states he sometimes wishes that the highly controversial technology would altogether disappear – not just from the video game industry, but from the world in its entirety. This makes sense, seeing as gen AI is now just about everywhere, from creative spaces to more technical areas like those involving coding or other forms of math and sciences. But, it's probably not going anywhere.

    According to recent reports, that's probably why Mikami actually uses it himself, as he admits he's experimented with AI – and continues to do so, too. Apparently, the legendary dev believes that utilizing the tech effectively can result in a higher-quality product without increasing the necessary budget. It, as the father of Resident Evil sees it, helps streamline production as well. That's not to say that Mikami's own newly introduced manufacturer, Unbound Studio, isn't overall "human-driven," though.

    Recent findings suggest that resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami claims he sometimes wishes AI would vanish entirely, not just from games, but from the world! However, he says he is right now experimenting with AI because effectively utilizing AI can yield higher quality within the same budget and streamline production. But for now, he says core tasks at his newly introduced Unbound Studio remain largely human-driven. He worries that five or ten years down the line there may be a real possibility of an era where developers might lose their jobs to AI. https://t.co/r6HIh5pgpmNovember 20, 2026.

    It is, according to Mikami, but it's difficult to consider, I suppose. It's different than what Shift Up CEO Kim Hyung-tae claims during the same interview – that Stellar Blade: Blood Rain is "handmade from start to finish" but still features AI – but the core of the whole 'AI is bad but I'm still using it' sentiment shines through similarly. Mikami does acknowledge the risk that the tech possibly poses to devs in the future, however.

    He's concerned that some five or ten years on, we could enter an era where devs actively lose their jobs to gen AI. It's an incredibly valid concern, all things considered (especially when you take the widespread layoffs ravaging the industry recently into account), but it does beg the question… Why use it, then? Would it not be contributing to his theorized problem? I guess it's hard to pinpoint – it may just be the fact that AI is popping up everywhere now.

    Kim himself thinks that working entirely without the worrisome tech isn't really feasible anymore as it's used in everything throughout development from simple quality assurance to more in-depth debugging. Sigh.

    Breaking: Steam's new Steam Deck framerate graphs are good news for handheld players, though I wouldn't fully trust the numbers yet

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (453 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck.
    • In a recent development, the thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide.
    • By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.

    In a recent development, the thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide. This may induce some gentle learned nodding, if you've ever tried an Unsupported game only to find it works more or less fine, or have ever wondered why a game that can just about scrape 30fps together gets the same green good-job sticker as something that screams along at 90fps. Now, when checking that rating, you'll also get a relatively specific idea of smoothness and/or chugging potential.

    Sources indicate that or will you? By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates. The scoundrel. My current handheld game beau, Mortal Shell II, looks like it may be falling victim to this: its results for the LCD Steam Deck show it mostly runs around 30fps, which is in line with my experience, but the OLED results show it averaging around 45fps. The Steam Deck OLED's APU is a tiny bit quicker than the LCD Deck's, but it's not that much of an upgrade.

    According to recent reports, there's work to be done, then, though I do appreciate the concept. As tightly as I cling to my battery-efficient, mercifully Windows-free Deck OLED in the face of drastically more powerful handhelds, with every year it becomes a little less likely that new games will comfortably run on it. Verification ratings can still act as decent (if broad) guidelines, but even with V-Sync putting an immaculately untorn thumb on the scales, game-specific framerate data will be much more illustrative.

    As for whether these histograms will also get Steam Machine versions, or perhaps cover non-Valve handhelds, Valve say this: "We see this update as a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck. To this end, we are also prompting customers to opt-in to providing anonymized framerate data in the Steam desktop client. This opt-in is currently only on Steam Client Beta, and will ship to all customers in the future." So, maybe, if you gizzus yer data.

    • Industry observers note that ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch.
    • Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a upcoming blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.
    • According to recent reports, we know that Season 2 is introducing a major upcoming map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the upcoming content and features coming with the new season.

    Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a upcoming blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

    According to recent reports, we know that Season 2 is introducing a major upcoming map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

    The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

    According to recent reports, challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

    BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

    Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

    In a recent development, movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

    It has been revealed that audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

    Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

    Sources indicate that in a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

    Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find new jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

    Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

    Sources indicate that this news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

    According to recent reports, diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

    The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

    The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

    The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

    What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s newly introduced region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

    Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two latest endgame modes in War Looks, and Echoing Hatred.

    Recent findings suggest that war Looks lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a upcoming activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

    Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

    Industry observers note that we also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

    According to recent reports, the Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first latest class in 25 years.

    Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Persona 4 Revival developers claim they were surprised that they had to "explicitly" say that the upcoming remake was based on the updated Persona 4 Golden rather than the base game. This is because they believed they'd dropped enough hints about the game in the original teaser trailer.

    In a recent development, in an interview with Famitsu, that's been translated by GamesRadar+, Persona series producer Kazuhisa Wada discusses how the team made a clear decision to base the upcoming ground-up remake on Persona 4 Golden from the very beginning. "Marie's story is woven through the main narrative," he explains. "So we made up our minds [to remake Persona 4 Golden rather than the original game] from the start. So don't be worried.".

    However, one of Persona 4's composers, Ryota Kozuka, was surprised that fans were ever confused as to which version of the game was being remade, as he thought there were enough hints in the teaser trailer. "As last year's teaser trailer used a song from Persona 4 Golden," he explains. "We thought the hints we used would get that across without saying it explicitly, but surprisingly there were a lot of people who didn't notice.".

    The teaser didn't show any Golden exclusive content such as Adachi's social link or the Velvet Room's Marie. However, some fans did spot that one of the Golden exclusive battle themes, Time to Make History, was used in the original trailer. There is also a split second where fans could see what looked like a covered scooter, a vehicle that is only found in the updated version.

    Many Persona fans, particularly those in the West, only joined the series starting with Persona 4 Golden. This means they never played the original game, which probably accounts for why many people missed out on this particular hint.

    "Persona 6 is not the end" for the series, lead hints, and Atlus is working to ensure fans "won't have to wait as long for the next game.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, in what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies.".

    If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting vital leverage from a global force.

    SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers.".

    Their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote.".

    Industry observers note that solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

    Nvidia's board of directors has reportedly met to decide whether to remove the tech giant's embattled CEO Jensen Huang, as news of a second extramarital affair has come to light.

    Per the Wall Street Journal, the board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang following reports he allegedly participated in another affair with an executive who worked for him.This followed the revelation of his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which prompted a organization-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation into whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

    The board's decision has yet to be made, but there are three expected outcomes. Either Huang stays with the firm and continues as Nvidia leader, despite the controversy or he is replaced as CEO, or he quits. Nvidia's share price dropped following reports of this meeting taking place.

    According to recent reports, if Huang is fired - and perhaps even if he isn't - it's likely to severely disrupt Nvidia's operations. Huang co-founded Nvidia and led it to become one of the world's most valuable companies - it interchangeably wears that crown, alternating with Apple. Replacing Huang might change the company's focus.

    Regardless, Nvidia is under major scrutiny right now because of Huang's actions. There are particular concerns around the firm's chips being imported to China despite trade bans. Gamers Nexus produced a documentary on the Nvidia AI GPU Black Market, detailing much of this.

    In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds.".

    GTA 6, of course, still does not have a confirmed PC version, even if Rockstar's former tech director states it's probably not far off. And despite this, even ancient, last-gen consoles are getting in on it, as the release also unexpectedly confirms that the game will be playable on Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming, Microsoft's game streaming service that has suddenly lost its ability to work on PC. Granted, this comes with a warning: "as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay." If you ended up getting a PS4 last generation, no cloud play for you either, I'm afraid. It also states that it will "play best on Playstation 5 consoles", making great use of that Sony partnership, and will include Playstation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro.

    A 2026 current-gen game targeting 30fps, let alone one as titanic of a release as GTA VI, is probably not going to go down well with a lot of people, even if console players are traditionally les sensitive about FPS counts than PC players. What this does imply, though, is that the inevitable PC release might be an even more demanding behemoth than expected, if Xbox Series and PS5 versions can't even target 60fps. The availability of the game on Xbox One, even if just through cloud streaming, could have resulted in an acceptance that 60fps just wasn't going to be possible if it was also going to be able to 'run' on last-gen hardware. Either way, when it does eventually escape console exclusivity, hopefully trying to run GTA VI on anything less than an RTX 5080 won't set your PC on fire. Now, let me just promptly have a glance at GPU prices. Oh, no.

    Tech Report: Will a Grand Theft Auto game ever be set outside of America? Rockstar offers a small glimmer of hope

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (376 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being.
    • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami.
    • In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then quickly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being. Across its history, there's only ever been one GTA game set outside America: the London-based expansion of the original game.

    Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami. But what about the next game - will the series always be in America? Not necessarily.

    In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then quickly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".

    Industry observers note that this is a topic Rockstar has responded to before, most notably when firm co-founder and long-time GTA writer Dan Houser - who's no longer at Rockstar - discussed why the series always seemed to return to America. He said it was because cities like Miami and Newly introduced York and Los Angeles are places where extreme juxtapositions exist. They're places where extreme wealth rubs shoulders with extreme poverty, and where organised crime can be found.

    There's also something America infamously has that few other countries do, and that's free availability of guns, which is such a core tenet of a GTA experience.

    Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, Obbe Vermeij - a former technical director at Rockstar North - revealed last year that a GTA: Tokyo almost happened. However, it wasn't going to be made by Rockstar but rather an external team in Japan.

    It has been revealed that while discussing the subject, Vermeij referred to America as "basically the epicenter of Western culture". "Everybody knows the cities, even people who haven't been there," Vermeij mentioned. "They have a mental image of the cities. I'm afraid we're stuck in this loop of about five American cities. Let's just get used to it.".

    Industry observers note that GTA 6 is just days away from its 19th November release on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar recently clarified the game runs at 30FPS across all platforms and confirmed that while it's available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, it cannot be streamed to PCs or non-Xbox devices.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nioh 3 has received a hot new enhancement that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific complications, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

    This latest upgrade, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

    There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for revision 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an concern that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

    This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an matter that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

    If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into concerns with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

    Recent findings suggest that team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

    If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an matter that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

    One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

    Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

    Industry observers note that hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.
